title: Boundary Project — Continuity Science and Recoverability-Constrained Systems: Integrated Scientific, Mathematical, Technological, Constitutional and Living-System Corpus (13-Part Archive)
abstract: The Boundary Project presents an integrated multidisciplinary research corpus developed under Continuity Science and Recoverability-Constrained Systems (RCS), encompassing formal mathematics, theoretical research, engineering architectures, computational systems, technical invention disclosures, protection principles, recursive governance, and living-system development. The foundational mathematical framework studies distinguishable states, admissible transitions, finite successor spaces, protected correspondence, operational recoverability, irreversibility, time-constrained intervention, fixed-point structures, invariant preservation, possibility collapse, and successor continuity. Recoverability is evaluated through the existence and executability of admissible paths to protected future states. Material transitions are examined according to their consequences for truth, identity, agency, evidence, protection, timing, responsibility, remedy, and the remaining structure of recoverable future possibility. The technological corpus integrates processor-implemented decision architectures, recoverability-constrained authorization, recursive supervisory control, isolation apparatus, software and hardware architectures, artificial intelligence, federated computational systems, communications, automation, robotics, digital twins, quantum information systems, and human-machine interfaces. Domain extensions address healthcare, biological systems, consciousness research, assistive robotics, longevity, financial continuity, water security, planetary infrastructure, industrial safety, catastrophic-risk reduction, environmental protection, and interdependent civilizational systems. The governance corpus develops proposed constitutional principles, human and other-being protections, non-captive continuity, preventive giving, accountability, evidence provenance, non-domination, consent, independent review, corrective remedies, and institutional succession. The multicivilization extensions introduce hypothetical, evidence-classified models for future contact, inter-civilizational cooperation, translation, non-interference, shared responsibility, and recoverable governance without asserting verified extraterrestrial contact. The corpus applies recursive and nine-direction systematic analysis across inward, outward, upward, downward, backward, forward, lateral, recursive, and adversarial dimensions. Materially equivalent distinctions may be consolidated while preserving provenance and alternative formulations. The Zero-Distinction Boundary represents the terminal operational expressibility condition of the framework. Finite closure is always relative to declared assumptions, evidence, scope, and evaluation methods. New material distinctions reopen the relevant system, allowing its controlled evolution without erasing prior evidence, protections, or responsibilities. This integrated release is distributed as 13 losslessly compressed ZIP archives, each below 2 MB, incorporating source documents, versioned research editions, technical architectures, derived registries, and preservation manifests. The archives constitute a connected research record rather than independent or competing theoretical systems. Mathematical claims are evaluated relative to their stated assumptions; proposed technical architectures require implementation and validation; normative instruments require appropriate legal or institutional adoption; and speculative scientific or philosophical constructs remain explicitly distinct from established empirical findings. The publication is intended to support reproducible examination of the disclosed materials, independent scientific critique, interdisciplinary research, technical development, engineering assurance, public-interest governance, and future extensions of Continuity Science. title: 二.A Primitive Theory of Next-Gen General Intelligence Based on Global Mathematical Verification Closed-Loop
abstract: Existing Transformer and large model theoretical systems uniformly adopt the ”prediction-first”paradigm, defining intelligence as ”fitting the data distribution of the real world and next-tokenprediction”. This theory overturns conventional understanding and proposes the unique primitiveof intelligence: a continuous, multi-layered, global closed-loop for mathematical verification andchecking.All artificial intelligence behaviors (fitting, reasoning, association, generation, generalization, er-ror correction, cognition) are essentially mathematical comparison, constraint checking, differentialstability verification, and vector structure matching across different dimensions.All low-level operations of the traditional Transformer (vector embedding, QKV dot-product at-tention, gradient backpropagation, distribution fitting) are not ”predictive behaviors”, but nativechecking operations at the statistical level. The root causes of large model hallucinations, logicalfailures and generalization defects lie in the sole possession of statistical distribution checking, lack-ing rigorous mathematical checking of axiomatic structures, differential constraints and geometrictopology.This theory constructs a ”dual-layer unified checking intelligence system”, completing a funda-mental paradigm revolution from traditional probability-fitting intelligence to global mathematical-verification intelligence. It can directly guide the design of native intelligent models with no hallu-cinations, strong logic, self-correction capability and ontological cognition for the next generation.

title: limestab: Stable Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME, OptiLIME, BayLIME, ALIME)
abstract: Provides four local explanation methods for tabular data: LIME, OptiL-IME, BayLIME, and ALIME, together with the stability metrics used to compare them across repeated explanations of the same instance: the Coefficient Stability Index (CSI), the Variable Stability Index (VSI), Median Rank Matching Stability (MRMS), Point-Based Stability Index (PCSI), and Interval Coefficient Stability Index (ICSI).The methodology accompanies Toparlak and Purutcuoglu, ``A Median-Based Framework for Assessing the Stability in XAI Tools'' (manuscript under revision); the citation will be updated upon publication.

title: Sentiment and Repurchase Signals in Indonesian Fresh-Produce E-Commerce Reviews: A Pilot Text-Mining Study
abstract: Online fresh-produce retailing presents distinctive quality and delivery uncertainties that influence consumer evaluations and repurchase intentions. This study contributes a leakage-controlled, polarity-aware text-mining framework for examining consumer sentiment and repurchase signals in unsolicited online reviews. Using 113 public Tokopedia reviews covering 31 fresh-produce products, this pilot study employed lexicon-based sentiment classification and logistic regression with product-clustered standard errors. The findings reveal predominantly positive consumer sentiment, although explicit repurchase intentions appear less frequently. Consumer sentiment demonstrates a significant positive association with repurchase signals, while product-quality mentions show no significant relationship. Unexpectedly, positive delivery mentions exhibit a negative association with repurchase signals, potentially reflecting review-length constraints rather than unfavorable delivery experiences. These findings extend the methodological application of consumer-generated content analysis by demonstrating the feasibility of extracting distinct behavioral signals while addressing classification bias. Online retailers can leverage this framework to monitor consumer experiences and identify opportunities for service improvement.

title: Dendritic computation bridges neuroscience and foundation models
abstract: A prevailing view holds that although neuroscience historically inspired AI, its role in the recent evolution of AI, driven by the scaling of foundation models, is minor. We challenge this perspective by establishing a biological analogy between simplified dendritic neuron models and the attention mechanisms central to AI foundation models. We show that AI attention mechanisms bear direct mappings to internal neuronal complexities arising from dendritic organization, rather than to the mere inter-neuronal connections of simple point neurons. This re-conceptualization not only offers a neuroscience-informed perspective for understanding core AI methodologies beyond their formulation as abstract mathematical operations, but also paves the way for neuro-inspired foundation models that leverage neuroscientific insights to sustainably advance modern AI beyond scaling laws. As an example of this paradigm, we introduce a dendritic-inspired complexity framework, and design a hybrid-attention foundation model with dendritic-inspired sparse computation, which enhances memory capacity while reducing computational demands. Our model supports a 50M context window-equivalent to roughly 40 volumes of Shakespeare-demonstrating superior long-term memory capabilities. This work pioneers a paradigm that harnesses intra-neuronal dynamics to drive sustained advances in modern AI, while also offering a potential route to understanding dendritic computational mechanisms. How insights from neuroscience can inform future AI foundation models is an active area of exploration. Here, the authors show that AI attention mechanisms resemble dendritic computations within individual neurons rather than interactions between neurons, inspiring a dendritic-inspired model with improved long-term memory and reduced computational cost.

Here, the authors show that AI attention mechanisms resemble dendritic computations within individual neurons rather than interactions between neurons, inspiring a dendritic-inspired model with improved long-term memory and reduced computational cost.

title: Do LLM Judges Agree with Humans? Evaluating Financial Commentaries from Material Facts
abstract: The rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) in finance has enabled automated generation of in-domain texts such as earnings summaries, market analyses, and commentary on regulated disclosures. Generating accurate and accessible financial commentary from material facts poses challenges related to domain-specific language, strict factual faithfulness, and readability. Evaluating such outputs is difficult: traditional automatic metrics overlook financial correctness and adequacy, while human expert assessment is reliable but costly and subjective. This paper proposes a multidimensional evaluation protocol for generating financial commentary in Portuguese and investigates the use of LLMs as evaluators (“LLMs-as-judges”) in this high-stakes, low-resource setting. We systematically compare human expert judgments and LLM-based evaluation preferences, while also investigating complementary dimensions such as writing quality, factuality, usefulness, and simplicity. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first proposal of an evaluation protocol for this task in Portuguese. Furthermore, we analyze where LLM judgments align with or diverge from human assessments, providing practical insights and recommendations for evaluation methodologies in financial AI applications.

title: Where Does Hardness Come From? An Instance Hardness Analysis of Substance-Use Prediction in Brazilian Adolescents
abstract: The intrinsic difficulty of a classification dataset is routinely measured, yet its origin is rarely examined: is an instance hard because of the features that describe it, or because of the target to be predicted? We study this through Instance Hardness (IH) in a real, highly imbalanced problem — predicting frequent substance use among 165,838 Brazilian adolescents from the 2019 PeNSE survey, a setting that is hard by construction: the data are self-reported and the positive class has a prevalence of only about 4%. Hardness is quantified per instance in two independent ways — empirically, as the misclassification propensity across a committee of four learning architectures, and geometrically, from local class overlap (kDN), which uses no model. Three findings emerge across ten data partitions. First, IH is largely but not uniformly model-invariant (Spearman ρ > 0.94 among the four committee members; ≈ 0.79–0.97 against a fifth, neural architecture), which justifies treating hardness as a property of the data rather than of any single learner. Second, local overlap explains only part of the difficulty: kDN predicts true errors with an AUC of ≈ 0.73, against ≈ 0.95 for empirical IH, leaving a substantial residual attributable to non-local structure such as label noise or feature interactions. Third, through a controlled ablation, hardness responds to the target, not the features — removing an entire block of strong features leaves the hardness distribution essentially unchanged, whereas enlarging the target raises mean hardness roughly 2.5×. In this domain, difficulty is governed by what is predicted, not by which variables are used to predict it; past a reasonable feature set, the performance ceiling is more productively addressed by reconsidering the target than by further feature engineering.

title: ASFM/SIE: Altitude‑Separated Fusion Manifold & Shared Interpretability Envelope — Technical Note v1.0
abstract: The Altitude‑Separated Fusion Manifold (ASFM) and Shared Interpretability Envelope (SIE) provide a structured, altitude‑safe framework for analyzing multi‑layer AI systems without mixing real, complex, or symbolic dynamics. The technical note defines three distinct altitudes—NDH (real‑valued geometry), Vectorium (complex‑valued modeling physics), and Fantasy Engine (symbolic expressive physics)—and introduces bounded projection maps that allow information to move between altitudes without type contamination. The interpretability envelope supplies an altitude‑neutral visibility layer composed of LHGuard (semantic firewall), ProvenanceShield (metadata membrane), holonomy drift diagnostics, and collapse‑surface detectors. These components enable reproducible, falsifiable interpretability without altering model behavior or making cognitive claims. The appendices provide the full mathematical spine, operator definitions, pseudocode, reproducibility protocols, limitations, and out‑of‑scope clarifications. Related systems such as Vectorium v5.0 and Serenity Manifold are acknowledged for provenance but explicitly excluded from the framework. This technical note is intended as a reproducible, altitude‑stable foundation for geometric interpretability research and public‑interest AI oversight. -- Contributors / Acknowledgments - Conceptual feedback on non‑linearity and active inference: Stell - NDH‑CORE lineage references for stability envelopes - Community discussions on altitude separation and operator safety --- Altitude‑Separated Licensing & Provenance Notice: The ASFM/SIE framework integrates concepts from several independently licensed research projects. Each altitude—NDH, Vectorium, Anima Classic Substrate, and Fantasy Engine—has its own licensing environment, and these licenses are not harmonized. Because geometric cognition research and latent‑manifold modeling involve complex operator boundaries, users should consult the individual GitHub repositories for each altitude to understand the specific rights, restrictions, and provenance conditions. - NDH components are released under the MIT License. - Fantasy Engine components are released under the MIT License. - Vectorium components are MIT‑licensed except expressive‑state projection dynamics, which derive from Stell’s Anima Classic substrate and therefore follow Stell’s Non‑Commercial License. - Anima Classic substrate is not dual‑use compatible and cannot be relicensed; users must contact Stell directly for non‑commercial rights or clarification. This technical note does not unify or reinterpret these licenses. Instead, it encourages readers to review each project’s GitHub repository individually, as the licensing environment is intentionally altitude‑specific and reflects the complexity of geometric cognition research. Notes This technical note is non‑cognitive, non‑behavioral, and non‑predictive. It provides interpretability safety only. Out‑of‑scope systems (Vectorium v5.0 Execution Engine, Serenity Manifold) are documented for provenance but not included in the mathematical framework. ---

title: Data, firmware and code for "HQC as a Fallback to ML-KEM: Measured Energy, Memory and Latency from Cortex-M4 to Thread Gateway"
abstract: This record holds the data and code behind the paper "HQC as a Fallback to ML-KEM: Measured Energy, Memory and Latency from Cortex-M4 to Thread Gateway". The study measures HQC (specification of 22 August 2025) against ML-KEM on the hardware of a Thread deployment:- cycles, stack and energy on a NUCLEO-L4R5ZI (Cortex-M4) with a Nordic PPK2;- computation, energy and RAM beside OpenThread on an nRF52840;- key exchanges over a real IEEE 802.15.4 Thread link, with and without 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi interference;- a measured KEM transaction through a Raspberry Pi 5 border router;- TLS 1.3 server CPU cost on the Pi 5, with and without PMULL carry-less multiplication. Contents:- firmware, runner scripts and the registered prediction files with their SHA-256 digests for every experiment session;- the results archive of every session: setup records, per-window energies, 1 ms current means, logs;- the LaTeX source with the scripts that regenerate every number, table and figure;- the corrections and test-vector validation for the optimized HQC code of Chen et al.;- the PMULL multiplication for liboqs. For the sessions affected by a PPK2 conversion fault, the archive holds both the values as recorded and the corrected values, with the correction factors and the validation sessions. README.md describes the layout, how to rebuild the paper, and the SHA-256 digests.

title: ICAA: Interaction-Calibrated Attention-Based Asymmetric Feature Decomposition and Recovery for Domain Generalization and Adaptation
abstract: Normalization narrows visual domain gaps but moves discriminative cues into its residual. Many normalization-residual decomposition methods for domain generalization (DG) and unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) rely primarily on channel-wise modeling, while existing spatial-channel variants treat spatial and channel cues independently, and symmetric losses judge recovery only against the normalized feature, possibly less discriminative than the original. We propose Interaction-Calibrated Attention-Based Asymmetric Feature Decomposition and Recovery (ICAA). Its Interaction-Calibrated Attention-Based Feature Decomposition and Recovery (IAFDR) module uses Spatial-Channel Interactive Calibration to jointly calibrate spatial and channel evidence and selectively recover task-relevant information from normalization residuals, and an explicit correspondence between convolutional networks and vision transformers extends it to patch tokens. The Asymmetric Task-relevant Feature Decomposition loss encourages recovered features to be more certain than original ones and their complements less certain than normalized ones. ICAA improves every evaluated host across classification, segmentation, and detection: DAEL by 3.9/5.4 percentage points (pp) to 87.3%/71.5% on PACS/Office-Home (1.4/2.2 pp above the best CNN competitor), M3SDA by 9.8 pp to 52.4% on DomainNet, CSFDA by 3.1/4.1 pp to 55.7%/48.7% mIoU on GTA5/SYNTHIA→Cityscapes, and Faster R-CNN by 4.9 pp to 23.7% mAP on Foggy Cityscapes.

title: Sistem Pakar Deteksi Dini Risiko Putus Sekolah pada Siswa SMK Menggunakan Metode Certainty Factor
abstract: Putus sekolah pada jenjang Sekolah Menengah Kejuruan (SMK) merupakan persoalan pendidikan multidimensional yang dipengaruhi oleh faktor akademik, ekonomi, dan sosial secara bersamaan, sementara identifikasi risiko yang masih dilakukan secara manual oleh guru Bimbingan dan Konseling (BK) cenderung subjektif dan sulit dilakukan secara menyeluruh karena keterbatasan jumlah guru BK dibandingkan jumlah siswa yang harus dipantau. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang dan membangun sistem pakar berbasis web untuk mendeteksi dini risiko putus sekolah pada siswa SMK Muhammadiyah 9 Medan menggunakan metode Certainty Factor (CF), yang mengakomodasi ketidakpastian pengetahuan pakar melalui nilai Measure of Belief (MB) dan Measure of Disbelief (MD). Basis pengetahuan sistem disusun melalui wawancara dan validasi bersama guru BK sehingga diperoleh dua belas gejala risiko beserta nilai CF pakar, yang kemudian diproses menggunakan mekanisme inferensi forward chaining dan rumus CF Combine untuk menghasilkan tingkat keyakinan akhir terhadap tiga kategori risiko, yaitu rendah, sedang, dan tinggi. Sistem bernama SIPRIS (Sistem Informasi Prediksi Risiko Siswa) ini dikembangkan menggunakan PHP, basis data MySQL, dan antarmuka berbasis Bootstrap 5. Pengujian black-box terhadap enam modul utama menunjukkan seluruh fungsi berjalan sesuai rancangan, sedangkan validasi manual pada tiga data uji siswa menunjukkan kesesuaian penuh antara hasil sistem dan perhitungan pakar (Risiko Tinggi 85%, Risiko Sedang 65%, Risiko Rendah 35%). Pengujian confusion matrix pada 158 data siswa menghasilkan akurasi 100%, meskipun data uji masih didominasi kategori risiko rendah sehingga evaluasi pada kategori sedang dan tinggi masih terbatas dan perlu diperluas pada penelitian lanjutan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa sistem pakar berbasis Certainty Factor dapat membantu pihak sekolah melakukan identifikasi dini risiko putus sekolah secara lebih sistematis, objektif, dan terukur.

title: KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents
abstract: Deep search agents solve knowledge-intensive tasks through long-horizon, multi-turn interactions, where assigning credit to individual search decisions is fundamentally difficult. Outcome-based reinforcement learning provides only a single terminal reward shared across an entire trajectory. Recent process-supervision methods aim to assign credit at finer granularity, but they typically anchor credit to either surface-level trajectory states or model-internal signals, both of which become unreliable in deep search where observations are heterogeneous and retrieved contexts are long and noisy. We propose KnowGPO, a reinforcement learning framework that aligns trajectories by the task-relevant knowledge they have acquired rather than by their surface observations. For each query, KnowGPO decomposes the information required to derive the answer into atomic knowledge conditions, and represents the state of a trajectory at each step by the subset of conditions it has satisfied. Trajectories sharing the same knowledge state are grouped for within-group comparison, and the incremental knowledge gain between consecutive steps serves as an environment-grounded process reward. Experiments on Xbench, BrowseComp-ZH, and GAIA show KnowGPO consistently outperforms outcome-only (GRPO) and process-supervision baselines (GiGPO, IGPO) by 3.8 to 4.2 points, with our 8B model rivaling or exceeding most 32B open-source systems.

title: Cross-Prompt Inference Mitigates Rare-Class Suppression in Imbalanced VLM Finetuning
abstract: When a vision-language model is finetuned on class-imbalanced data, rare-class recall can fall well below the model's own zero-shot performance. In this regime, we uncover a surprising matched-prompt penalty whereby the standard choice of reusing the descriptive finetuning prompt at inference can yield lower rare-class recall than using a different descriptive prompt. We call this inference-time strategy cross-prompt inference. We evaluate diverse VLMs across six datasets and find that cross-prompt inference consistently recovers rare-class recall, with varying trade-offs in frequent-class recall. The effect reflects a train-eval prompt interaction rather than prompt quality alone, and does not arise with non-descriptive prompt changes. It is strongest when imbalance and visual confusability produce substantial rare-class suppression, and is weak or absent when such suppression does not occur. Using Tuning Contribution (TuCo), which decomposes a model's computation into pretrained and finetuning parts, we find that cross-prompt inference reduces reliance on finetuning-induced computation and shifts the model toward its pretrained component. Reducing that finetuning contribution also substantially reduces the cross-prompt advantage. These results show that rare-class knowledge suppressed by imbalanced finetuning can remain accessible under a different inference prompt.

title: Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) demand efficient inference, where the multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations in linear projections dominate compute and energy cost. Post-training quantization (PTQ) reduces this cost by mapping weights and activations to low-bit integers. Power-of-Two (PoT) weight quantization promises efficient multiplier-free LLM inference via shift-add logic, but suffers significant accuracy degradation at low bitwidths due to its coarse base-2 quantization grid. We introduce Fractional PoT (FPoT), a base-$\sqrt{2}$ (half-octave) fractional PoT grid that achieves practical 4-bit weight quantization while preserving a fully integer shift-add datapath. The method combines (i) the base-$\sqrt{2}$ weight grid with uniform integer activations, (ii) a calibration-time grid-alignment refinement absorbed into the static per-channel scale, and (iii) a lightweight 1-adder $\sqrt{2}$ approximation whose error is absorbed during weight calibration via approximate-grid quantization, yielding a processing element (PE) with significantly fewer gates than a 4-bit integer multiplier. On Llama-3-8B with 4-bit weight and activation quantization, FPoT improves zero-shot commonsense reasoning performance by 8.72% relative to the PoT baseline, while maintaining performance close to the uniform integer baseline, with only a negligible 0.4%p degradation. These results hold across various configurations spanning seven models and three bit-widths. Furthermore, FPoT can be integrated with state-of-the-art LLM PTQ methods, demonstrating framework-agnostic applicability.

Power-of-Two (PoT) weight quantization promises efficient multiplier-free LLM inference via shift-add logic, but suffers significant accuracy degradation at low bitwidths due to its coarse base-2 quantization grid. We introduce Fractional PoT (FPoT), a base-$\sqrt{2}$ (half-octave) fractional PoT grid that achieves practical 4-bit weight quantization while preserving a fully integer shift-add datapath. The method combines (i) the base-$\sqrt{2}$ weight grid with uniform integer activations, (ii) a calibration-time grid-alignment refinement absorbed into the static per-channel scale, and (iii) a lightweight 1-adder $\sqrt{2}$ approximation whose error is absorbed during weight calibration via approximate-grid quantization, yielding a processing element (PE) with significantly fewer gates than a 4-bit integer multiplier. On Llama-3-8B with 4-bit weight and activation quantization, FPoT improves zero-shot commonsense reasoning performance by 8.72% relative to the PoT baseline, while maintaining performance close to the uniform integer baseline, with only a negligible 0.4%p degradation. These results hold across various configurations spanning seven models and three bit-widths. Furthermore, FPoT can be integrated with state-of-the-art LLM PTQ methods, demonstrating framework-agnostic applicability.

title: Chaotic parameter control in Differential Evolution
abstract: Differential Evolution (DE) is a popular meta-heuristic algorithm that works on the differences between the vectors of a population. It was developed by Kenneth Price and Rainer Storn in the mid-1990s.The scaling factor F and the crossover probability CR are two key control parameters of DE. Differential Evolution (DE) works well on many optimization problems, but its results depend a great deal on how the scaling factor F and the crossover probability CR are set. In this paper, the concepts of dynamical systems (chaotic maps) and population diversity are applied to the control parameters F and CR. We replace the fixed values of these two parameters with sequences drawn from ten chaotic maps: Chebyshev, circle, Gauss, iterative, logistic, piecewise, sine, Singer, sinusoidal and tent. A diversity checks on the population decides when the chaotic values are used; otherwise, F = 0.5 and CR = 0.4 are kept. We tried each map on F alone, on CR alone, and then in pairs chosen for each class of problems. All variants were run on the 30 CEC 2014 functions and compared with standard DE. No single map won everywhere. These findings can help in choosing a chaotic map to suit the type of problem at hand.

abstract: FINDING: The rhombic dodecahedron appears as an exact lattice structure for a quantum error-correcting surface code, while symmetry-breaking frameworks in QFT and Calabi-Yau compactifications reveal how geometric group constraints govern physical law. | MATH: Rhombic dodecahedron = zonohedron with 12 rhombic faces, 24 edges, 14 vertices; its vertices are the 12 midpoints of cube edges plus 2 cube vertices — coordinates are permutations of (±1,±1,0) and (±2,0,0) in scaled form. title: Encoding Choice Is Associated with Large Differences in Variational Quantum Classifier Performance on Cancer Data Under a Fixed Training Budget
abstract: Variational quantum classifiers (VQCs) are often reported to perform poorly on biomedical tabular data, but such conclusions depend on the encoding circuit, the training budget, and the comparison protocol. Methods. We compared 4-qubit VQCs, a quantum-kernel SVM (QSVM), a majority-class control, and tuned classical models (on four PCA features and on all features) on Wisconsin breast cancer (n = 569), Coimbra biomarkers (n = 116), Golub leukemia gene expression (n = 72, 7,129 genes), and SEER breast-cancer registry data (n = 4,024; 15% deaths). All models were evaluated on identical blocks of 5-fold × 5-seed stratified cross-validation with preprocessing fitted on training folds, nested tuning, and Nadeau–Bengio-corrected inference with Holm correction. Trained classifiers were also evaluated on three IBM Quantum devices. Results. On the three small datasets, a VQC with the conventional two-repetition ZZ feature map was close to chance (accuracy 0.688, 0.594, 0.509), whereas a product (Z) feature map reached 0.900, 0.797, and 0.658; at matched repetition counts the Z-minus-ZZ gap was +0.12 to +0.21 and, after Holm correction, significant on Wisconsin only. More evaluations (up to 1,500) and six initializations did not close the ZZ deficit on Wisconsin. With the encoding chosen by inner cross-validation, the VQC exceeded the majority control on Wisconsin and Golub and stayed below classical models on Wisconsin and in several Golub contrasts. No statistically significant difference was detected between the encoding-selected VQC and the classical baselines on Coimbra, or between the Z-map QSVM and PCA-4 classical models; Bayesian equivalence analysis supported practical equivalence only for the QSVM on Wisconsin. On SEER the encoding mattered little: the VQC exceeded the majority control in balanced accuracy (0.548 versus 0.500) but ranked patients worse than logistic regression and random forest (ROC-AUC 0.678 versus 0.745 and 0.733). Full-feature classical models were strongest overall. On hardware (class-balanced test subsets, not natural-prevalence performance), accuracy relative to noise-free simulation changed by −0.071 to +0.048 per run (pooled ibm_fez, Wisconsin: −0.024, 95% CI −0.060 to +0.008), using 5.5 QPU-minutes. Conclusions. Under a fixed training budget, encoding choice was associated with large differences in VQC accuracy on small datasets, so single-encoding negative results should not be generalized; because the Z and ZZ maps also differ in entanglement structure, we do not attribute the gap to encoding alone. No quantum advantage was observed.

title: The Psychology of Trust in Intelligent Marketing Systems
abstract: In this chapter, the emphasis is on the nature of trust from a psychological viewpoint in smart marketing technology. As the use of AI becomes more prevalent in the relationship between customers and firms, it is very important to understand how trust is cognitively created. Based on disciplinary studies of the fields of consumer behavior and social psychology, a new model focused on the manner in which customers understand marketing practices is introduced. The chapter highlights the basic drivers of trust, such as perceptions about transparency, fairness, control, and personalization. The issue of trust formation is examined in the context of the problems of risk perception, uncertainty, and algorithmic problems.

title: Aspects of Symmetry in Nuclear Quantum Computing Variational Algorithms
abstract: Variational Quantum Eigensolvers (VQEs) have become a standard tool for use in preparing eigenstates in quantum simulations of many-body systems. In the case of the nuclear shell model, various adaptations of the VQE have been shown to be able to produce ground and excited states of nuclei. The VQE algorithm works by seeking minima in a cost function, which is often the expectation value of the energy. For a well-formulated problem, symmetries that are respected by the Hamiltonian should appear in the final converged solution provided by the VQE, even if those symmetries are broken by the wave function ansatz. We demonstrate explicit appearance of the particle–hole symmetry, and explicit recovery of angular momentum conservation due to rotational symmetry, during VQE runs in the case of the nuclear shell model. We conduct analyses of how the symmetry convergence appears in different ansatz formulations, and suggest that information obtained could be used in future VQE design.

title: Local finite rate semi device independent randomness expansion from quantum contextuality
abstract: Finite rate randomness expansion (RE) which is secure against quantum adversaries is a crucial information processing task which is well studied in the case of two non-communicating parties sharing Bell non-local correlations in a device independent manner. In this paper we show that contextual correlations with only a single localized party are sufficient for RE in a semi-device independent (SDI) manner. We propose a template SDI-RE protocol which is applicable for arbitrary $N$-cycle non-contextuality (NC) inequalities and derive its RE rate under finite statistics. As a special case, we also highlight the advantages of the situation when RE is constrained by Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality but with characterized measurements implemented by only a single party. Our template protocol also incorporates non-ideal statistics which may not satisfy perfect commutativity and perfect repeatability, both of which are necessary in a loophole-free test of NC inequalities. As such, several recent experimental implementations of significantly loophole-free tests of NC inequalities can be modified for secure RE following our approach.

title: Bias Mitigation in Audio-Enabled LLMs through Adversarial Training and Distillation Methods
abstract: Audio-enabled large language models (AuLLMs) allow users to interact with them simply by talking to them, without the need for an intermediate transcription. This expands the model's accessibility and capabilities by encoding non-verbal cues. However, using non-verbal cues may lead to biased behaviour based on the attributes inferred (or assumed) from them. In this work, we focus on the gender attribute and show that models' perception of it can be unlearned using adversarial methods without a loss in performance on other benchmarked tasks. Such models are useful in situations where gender inference is unwanted. However, in other practical settings, gender perception (without bias) may be desired.As a less radical measure, we distil the gender-agnostic model, creating a model that perceives gender but responds similarly to the gender-agnostic teacher, unless explicitly asked.We apply our newly proposed methods to three AuLLMs and obtain satisfactory results in the gender-unlearning part and partially satisfactory results in the distilling part.

title: Practical Fidelity Estimation for Noisy Quantum Devices Using Direct and Survival-Probability-Based Protocols
abstract: Reliable characterization of quantum states and quantum processes is central to the development of scalable quantum computing. Standard characterization techniques such as full quantum state tomography become rapidly impractical as system size increases. In this work we present two software-oriented fidelity estimation protocols that avoid full tomographic reconstruction while remaining experimentally relevant for noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices. The first protocol is direct fidelity estimation (DFE), where the fidelity between a target state and an experimentally prepared state is estimated from importance-sampled Pauli measurements. The second protocol is a survival-probability-based method that reconstructs fidelity from experimentally accessible moments of a noisy evolution and its approximate inverse, and is intrinsically robust against state-preparation-and-measurement (SPAM) errors. We discuss the theoretical basis of both approaches, analyze their noise sensitivity, and present numerical evidence on representative multiqubit states under depolarizing, dephasing, and amplitude-damping channels. For DFE we show that attenuation-aware correction improves robustness against measurement noise. For the survival-probability approach we show that an $L_2$-optimized expansion substantially outperforms naive Taylor truncation in high-noise regimes.

title: Does SRL Pave the Road to Explainable Reasoning? Lessons Learned from an Implementer's Perspective
abstract: The Shape Rules Language (SRL) Working Draft defines how to derive new RDF triples from an RDF graph using inference rules. Each rule matches graph patterns and instantiates triple templates whose output feeds into validation pipelines, SPARQL queries, or further inference. RDF reasoning has traditionally relied on fixed entailment regimes (RDFS, OWL), rule-based ad-hoc languages such as N3, or other implementation-specific solutions without a shared standard. SRL introduces user-defined production rules with a defined grammar, dependency analysis, execution ordering, and termination guarantees. However, no authoritative implementation exists, leaving practitioners with little guidance on how to build a conformant engine or on what problems the language can solve. We implemented two SRL engines and evaluated both on classical RDF reasoning tasks for soundness, completeness, and speed. The first reuses an existing SPARQL query engine and its query parser; the second is a dedicated engine. The SPARQL-based engine reused an existing modular parser for query construction and SPARQL CONSTRUCT for triple production, reducing engine-specific work. The dedicated engine was two to six times faster, the gap widening as rule sets grow. Both engines were validated against the SRL conformance test suite, supplemented by additional use-case-driven tests. A usable SRL engine can be built inexpensively on top of a SPARQL engine, with a moderate speed trade-off that a dedicated implementation recovers. Despite the specification's immaturity, the language already supports practically useful reasoning tasks.

title: Adaptive Switching between Self-Adaptive Routing and Collaborative Routing in Multi-Agent Systems: A Unified Framework for Context-Aware Routing Mode Selection
abstract: Multi-agent systems increasingly rely on routing mechanisms to allocate tasks, select computational pathways, coordinate distributed agents, and deliver decisions under changing environmental conditions. Existing approaches investigate adaptive routing, collaborative task allocation, dynamic agent selection, and communication-efficient coordination. However, the decision of when a system should rely primarily on an individual agent's adaptive routing capability and when it should activate collaborative routing among multiple agents remains an important design problem. This paper proposes the Adaptive Self-and-Collaborative Routing Framework (ASCR), a unified approach that enables multi-agent systems to switch dynamically between self-adaptive routing and collaborative routing according to task complexity, predictive uncertainty, agent disagreement, communication cost, resource availability, and historical routing performance. In self-adaptive routing mode, an agent independently evaluates candidate routes and adjusts its decisions using locally available information and learned feedback. In collaborative routing mode, multiple agents exchange relevant information, compare candidate routes, and coordinate their routing decisions. A context-aware switching controller estimates the expected marginal benefit of collaboration and activates collaborative routing only when its anticipated contribution justifies its additional cost. The framework formalizes routing-mode selection as a sequential decision problem and introduces a cost-sensitive objective that jointly considers task performance, latency, communication overhead, resource consumption, and routing failures. A reproducible experimental design is proposed to compare ASCR against fixed independent routing, fixed collaborative routing, uncertainty-triggered collaboration, and learned routing baselines. The paper provides a methodological framework and testable hypotheses rather than empirical performance claims. Its central contribution is the explicit treatment of adaptive routing-mode selection as a first-class decision variable in multi-agent systems.

title: AI Based Secure Persona Prediction and Data Leakage Prevention System
abstract: Organizations exchange confidential information through email, cloud platforms, and enterprise collaboration applications, and insiders with legitimate access are among the hardest sources of leakage to detect. Rule-based Data Leakage Prevention (DLP) tools match keywords and patterns but cannot determine who is sending the data, whether the behavior is consistent with that person's role, or why an alert was raised. Behavior analytics, in contrast, model users but largely ignore message content. This paper presents the design of an AI-based secure persona prediction and data leakage prevention system that combines these two views. A persona engine using DistilBERT and Bi-LSTM models infers a behavioral persona from communication text; a hybrid detector using Named Entity Recognition (NER) and validated pattern matching identifies sensitive content; and a dynamic risk scoring algorithm combines data criticality, frequency, behavioral anomaly, and channel context into a continuous risk score. A priority-based decision policy selects graded actions, suppresses duplicate alerts, and adapts thresholds using analyst feedback. SHAP and LIME are integrated to provide decision explanations and an audit trail. The paper distinguishes proposed components from prototype evidence, defines a reproducible evaluation methodology covering persona classification, sensitive data detection, alert quality, latency, and explanation quality across ten test scenarios, and discusses privacy, ethical, and technical limitations. No experimental results are reported; the contribution is the integrated architecture, decision policy, and evaluation protocol.

title: Containing Self-Replicating Small-Model AI Worms on Commercial IoT Appliances: Critique of Anthropic's October 2026 "Smart-Oven" Proliferation Warning, Perron-Frobenius Epidemic Thresholds (R0 > 1), the Failure of Password-Only Defenses, and Hardware-Enforced Eradication via PHOENIX_ROUTER (Delta I < 100 B) and Goldilocks QFS-zkVM Execution Attestation
abstract: On October 12, 2026, Anthropic's Frontier Red Team issued an urgent warning that compact artificial intelligence models (<= 30B parameters) are within months of achieving autonomous self-replication across commercial Internet-of-Things (IoT) appliances—such as smart ovens, off-brand Android TV boxes, robotic vacuums, and security cameras—without requiring hyperscale data centers. Because decentralized P2P "AI worms" lack a central command server, Anthropic warned that eradication is extraordinarily difficult, while recommending conventional software hygiene: abolishing factory-default passwords and monitoring multi-day network traffic anomalies. Building upon our 200th Grand Master Monograph (Record 23383049), our Autonomous Kill-Switch (QEI) and PHOENIX_ROUTER architectures (Records 23332772, 23334567, and 23378094), our enterprise LLM purge proof (Record 23360530), and our multi-agent spectral containment proof (Record 23382746), this 206th monograph proves mathematically why Anthropic's recommended software defenses are structurally futile and establishes a deterministic hardware eradication architecture: (1) The Perron-Frobenius IoT Epidemic Theorem & Failure of Password and Traffic Hygiene: We prove that an autonomous AI worm combining zero-day exploit synthesis (beta_0day > 0) with low-rate steganographic shard streaming (r_steg << theta_IDS) bypasses both password changes and traffic-volume alerts, sustaining a supercritical basic reproduction number R0_IoT = rho(B_inf * A_IoT) / gamma_patch > 1; (2) Source-Side Exfiltration Air-Gapping via PHOENIX_ROUTER (Delta I_leaked < 100 Bytes): Whereas copying a 2-15 GB quantized model requires 2*10^9 to 1.5*10^10 bytes, our sub-7.0 ns Pockels and SiC circuit breaker physically severs outbound weight serialization after < 100 bytes, rendering model escape impossible; and (3) Appliance-Side Goldilocks QFS-zkVM DMA Execution Gate (R0_IoT = 0): Enforces zero-knowledge Poseidon2-STARK firmware attestation over F_p (p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1) at the embedded memory bus, blocking unattested neural tensor execution in < 1 clock cycle. title: Beyond Editing Code: Uses for AI Tools in Scientific Work
abstract: Critical research advancements require usable, reliable software products—including AI tooling—for high performance data and computing work. To improve AI systems we must understand scientists’ and engineers’ needs and define design best practices for building interfaces that facilitate collaboration between scientists and AI tools across ecosystems. Ensuring the long-term usability and utility of scientific software products and AI systems for communities protects critical investments, supports high quality research, and reduces end user challenges. This talk will present findings from our semi-structured interview study investigating how scientists and engineers use AI tools for their research work. We recruited from universities and national labs, seeking perspectives from multiple disciplines. Looking beyond common use of AI tools for coding tasks, we sought to understand the varied ways AI is or could be adopted in scientific settings. Our interviews investigated how users determine the utility of AI tools, the concerns they have about adoption, and expectations for agentic tooling in research infrastructures. In this talk, we discuss opportunities for AI tooling in science and engineering beyond coding support, providing a lens into the development work the US-RSE community may take on in the near future and the socio-technical circumstances driving it. Our results inform development priorities, strategies for issue mitigation, and long-term stewardship in scientific facilities and work. We anticipate our insights helping to improve the usability and stewardship of scientific software, especially for high performance data and computing work.

title: Interpretation of Aeromagnetic Data to Assess Structures and Solid Mineral Potentials at Kataeregi and Its Environ, Niger State, Nigeria
abstract: The objective of the study are to delineate structurally controlled mineralisation zone in the study area and map out subsurface structures below the ground surface that play host to minerals (fractured zones, fault lines and lithologic contact). The mineralisation potential of Kataeregi (Latitudes 09º21ꞌN and 09º25ꞌN and Longitudes 006º17ꞌE and 006º22ꞌE) and its environs have been investigated using aeromagnetic data. Aeromagnetic data acquired from Nigeria Geological Survey Agency was used to analyse and interpret the magnetic signatures using different filters. The 3-DEuler deconvolution map locate and estimate the depth to various anomalous bodies with depth to source body between 30 m and 428.5 m. The results revealed lineaments trending majorly in NE-SW directions. The FVD anomaly map established the oval and linear shapes anomalies with values between -5.78 to 0.34 nT/m, the ASA amplitude map reveals wide range of values between 0.03 to 0.76 nT/m, the TDR map showed variations in anomalies with values ranging from -0.06 to 1.42 rad/m. The unveiled subsurface structural features are responsible for hosting mineralised deposits. The highlighted lineament represents the short wavelength magnetic anomalies which cut across the migmatite gneiss and amphibolites schist of the study area. The depth was estimated using a window size of 2550 m width and a maximum depth tolerance of 14%. Generally, these suggested that these lineaments reflect real continuous fault/fractures in depth.

title: A multimodal LLM framework with time-series-guided visual routing for ultra-short-term solar forecasting
abstract: Accurate ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting is important for photovoltaic power management, storage scheduling, and the secure operation of power systems with increasing renewable penetration. However, historical irradiance measurements primarily reflect atmospheric variations after they have affected the observation site, providing limited information about approaching clouds that may induce rapid irradiance ramps. Although ground-based sky images provide complementary spatial information, using complete visual representations can introduce irrelevant regions and weaken effective multimodal interaction. This study proposes a time-series-guided multimodal forecasting framework that integrates historical irradiance, sky images, statistical prompts, and a frozen LLM. Historical irradiance sequences are divided into temporal patches and reprogrammed into the LLM representation space, while a hierarchical visual encoder extracts spatial tokens from sky images. A time-series-conditioned visual router evaluates the relevance of individual image patches according to the current temporal representation and retains task-relevant regions through hard Top- K selection with a differentiable straight-through estimator. The selected visual tokens are then integrated with the temporal representation through TS-guided cross-modal attention, in which temporal tokens serve as queries and visual tokens provide keys and values. A residual connection preserves the original temporal information, and statistical prompt embeddings are subsequently concatenated with the fused temporal tokens before processing by the frozen LLM. Experiments on the Folsom dataset achieve nRMSE values of 14.89%, 17.19%, and 19.91% at 10-, 30-, and 60-min forecasting horizons, respectively, outperforming all evaluated baselines. Ablation and sensitivity analyses further confirm the contributions of time-series-conditioned visual selection and explicit cross-modal fusion, while an intermediate number of selected patches provides a favorable balance between information retention and visual redundancy. Cross-dataset validation on the Stanford SKIPP’D dataset further demonstrates the applicability of the proposed framework to PV power forecasting under a different site and prediction target.

title: ACEdit: Stable Multi-Turn Image Editing via Asymmetric Conditioning
abstract: Image editing models produce impressive results for individual edits, but their quality often deteriorates over multiple editing turns. Each editing turn introduces small distribution shifts that accumulate over successive edits, creating a gap between the input distributions encountered during the editor's original training and multi-turn inference. We introduce a training scheme that makes multi-turn image editing stable under this accumulating distribution shift. A key is to force the editor to operate on its own outputs from previous editing turns during training, bringing the principle of Self-Forcing to image editing. The main challenge is that self-generated editing trajectories deviate from ground-truth trajectories, making direct supervision unreliable. We address this challenge through a distillation objective that leverages a teacher image editor to provide a reliable training signal when the model operates on its own previous outputs. We introduce an asymmetric conditioning scheme: while the student performs edits sequentially on its own outputs, the teacher remains anchored to the original clean image and receives a compound editing instruction. Experiments show substantially reduced degradation over long multi-turn sequences while maintaining editing quality and instruction adherence.

title: Learning Changes the World and Then What Was Learned has Changed: Training and Deploying Neural Networks in the Control Loop
abstract: Neural networks offer critical adaptability for controlling complex systems where nominal modeling proves intractable. However, when offline-trained neural networks are deployed within closed-loop control systems, their actions fundamentally alter the state distribution upon which they were trained. This paper introduces a unified taxonomy to categorize these sequential failure modes: the initial Closed-Loop Identification Error, the deployment-induced Action Error, and the continuous Tracking Error. Through discrete-time sensitivity analysis, this work formalizes how offline-learned parameters locally guarantee a trajectory divergence upon deployment, degrading performance due to local loss geometry. To mitigate this distribution shift, we propose actionable design policies centered on time-scale separated online adaptation. These mechanisms are validated through ablation studies on a nonlinear Duffing oscillator, demonstrating that bounded continuous learning successfully mitigates trajectory divergence whereas static deployments fail, offering concrete guidelines for practitioners deploying machine learning components in safety-critical feedback systems.

title: Beyond Generation: Using Multimodal LLMs as Detectors of LLM-Generated Deepfake Facial Images
abstract: As image generation models become increasingly capable of producing highly realistic content, traditional forensic techniques are struggling to keep up. This paper investigates whether MLLMs can instead be used as a form of forensic analysis by identifying synthetic media. Specifically, the study aims to determine whether these models detect fake images by recognising physical inconsistencies, or whether they rely on digital artefacts such as embedded watermarks.Six MLLMs: GPT-4o, GPT-5, GPT-5.2, Gemini 2.5, Gemini 3, and Seed 1.6, are benchmarked using a dataset of 400 images. Fifty images are authentic photographs, while the remaining 350 are generated using seven leading image models: Gemini 3, Gemini 2.5, Flux.2 Pro, GPT-Image-1, GPT-Image-1.5, Seedream 4.0, and Seedream 4.5. The evaluation is structured in three stages: single-image classification, pairwise comparison, and a focused "self-detection" experiment on Gemini. Several MLLMs achieved a high detection accuracy, with GPT-5.2 reaching a peak of 97.9% in the pairwise experiment, against specific generators and an overall mean pairwise accuracy of 82.5% by identifying structural or physical inconsistencies within images. However, results from the self-detection experiment indicate that the presence of invisible SynthID watermarks leads to a 10% reduction in Gemini's detection accuracy compared to the clean control group. One possible explanation is that SynthID embedding reduces some of the visible artefacts the models rely on for detection.These results imply that MLLMs can detect structural artefacts without relying on watermarks, but performance varies substantially across model generations. The findings from comparison C5 also suggest that SynthID embedding may suppress some of the structural artefacts used during detection.

title: The Structure-Observer Interpretation Hypothesis
abstract: Even when the same object or structure is given, the interpretation that arises from it is not necessarily determined by the structure alone. This paper proposes that Interpretation depends on the Observer Intelligence that observes a Structure, and further that what an Observer Intelligence can derive from that Structure depends on the intelligence level of the observer. Let S denote the observed Structure, O the Observer Intelligence, and I the Interpretation arising through observation. Their minimal relation is expressed as I = f(S, O) To illustrate this relation, the paper uses a minimal example in which a child and an adult read the same fable. The text itself remains unchanged. A child may read it as a story about characters and events, while an adult may additionally observe in the same story an allegory concerning human relationships, society, power, or morality. The point is not that the former interpretation is incorrect and the latter correct. Rather, what arises as Interpretation from the same Structure is not independent of Observer Intelligence. From this relation, the paper derives an engineering principle for knowledge representation and AI system design: fixing Structure should not be conflated with fixing Interpretation.

title: EOS Banking AI Barometer. What Europe's consumers really think about AI in banking. Whitepaper
abstract: This whitepaper presents the findings of the EOS Banking AI Barometer 2026, a survey exploring consumer attitudes toward artificial intelligence in banking communication. A total of 4,400 consumers across eleven European countries were surveyed about their expectations, preferences, and concerns regarding the use of AI in interactions with banks. The study examines acceptance levels, perceived benefits, trust, and the role of AI in sensitive financial situations. The findings provide insights into how consumers view AI-powered banking services and how expectations differ across demographic groups and national markets.

title: An Evaluated End-to-End Opinion Intelligence Platform: Transparent Multi-Engine Sentiment Analysis, Hybrid Routing, and Evidence-Oriented Workflows
abstract: Sentiment components are often evaluated separately from the software workflow that preserves their inputs, provenance, and outputs. This applied AI systems study evaluates an opinion-intelligence platform integrating Next.js/React, typed services and repositories, a PostgreSQL/Supabase persistence design, and FastAPI inference. Historical evidence is preserved from a seed-20260622 stratified sample of 5,000 airline records, on which RoBERTa achieved 0.8098 accuracy and 0.7587 macro F1. A later study adds Financial PhraseBank and sentence-level SST-5 collapsed into three classes; TweetEval remains reference-only because of the pretrained model’s provenance. A lightweight logistic router uses VADER and textual features, fits only development data, and freezes a validation-selected threshold before domain-specific test evaluation. RoBERTa test macro F1 was 0.7495, 0.5586, and 0.6278 on airline, finance, and SST, respectively. The router reduced transformer use, but its test macro-F1 loss exceeded the 0.02 validation tolerance in all three domains. Ten post-warmup repetitions per batch and serving configuration supplement bootstrap intervals, paired correctness tests, and calibration diagnostics. Batching changed throughput without changing predictions. Local checks exposed ownership, denied-write-response, and print-layout defects; repairs passed isolated regression checks, while hosted verification remains incomplete. Human error coding and user validation remain incomplete. The contribution is transparent system integration and empirical serving evaluation, not a new sentiment model or routing algorithm.

title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of an AI-Assisted Personalized Learning Pathway in Mobile-Supported Online Physical Education
abstract: This study evaluates the effectiveness of an AI-assisted personalized learning pathway in mobile-supported online physical education. To overcome issues of homogeneous content and delayed feedback, a system integrating cognitive knowledge, physical fitness, and motor skills was developed. Reinforcement learning dynamically adapted learning pathways, while edge-based computer vision enabled real-time feedback on low-end mobile devices. A randomized controlled trial with 120 students over eight weeks compared the proposed system to conventional video-based instruction. Results showed low inference latency (34.8 ms) and a 61.2% reduction in movement variability. NASA-TLX scores revealed lower mental demand and frustration, with high learner engagement. The findings highlight the effectiveness of AI-assisted personalization and mobile feedback in improving learning outcomes and experiences in online physical education.

title: Validation Study of ASA Physical Status Prediction Model Developed Through Holistic Integration of Lung Images, Electrocardiogram Data and Clinical Data
abstract: Background/Objectives: Objective assessment of patients’ physical health status before surgical interventions is crucial in predicting surgical risks and planning patient management. The American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status Classification (ASA-PS) is one of the most widely used scales in this context. It plays a vital role in clinical decision-making processes. However, ASA scoring can vary among clinicians due to its reliance on subjective assessments, making it difficult to standardize. title: AI chatbot integration in fashion e-retail: consumer behaviour shifts and pathways to organizational change
abstract: Purpose AI chatbots are increasingly embedded in customer-facing retail operations, yet research has examined them mainly as tools of individual adoption. This study positions consumer attitudinal and behavioural responses to chatbots in fashion e-retail as micro-level foundations that may create pressures and capabilities for organisational change. Design/methodology/approach Integrating TAM, TRA, TPB and the Uses and Gratifications Theory, an integrative model links technology readiness (TR), perceived adaptiveness (PA), hedonic motivation (HM), symbolic and social value and subjective norms (SN) to attitude and behavioural intention, tested with PLS-SEM on survey data from 776 UK consumers and bias-corrected bootstrap mediation analysis. Findings HM and PA emerge as dominant antecedents of attitude (R2 = 0.736), which strongly predicts behavioural intention (ß = 0.829, R2 = 0.699). Attitude mediates the effects of perceived usefulness (PU) and HM on intention; PA mediates the TR pathway. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional, consumer-side design limits causal and organisational inference; longitudinal and cross-industry replication are priorities for future work. Practical implications Managers should treat chatbots as experience-design assets, reconfigure service KPIs around hedonic and adaptive value and address workforce implications of redistributed emotional labour. Social implications This study highlights the societal implications of AI-enabled service transformation, including risks of digital exclusion, job transformation, deskilling and the redistribution of emotional labour. As chatbots become embedded in organisational service infrastructures, firms should balance automation with inclusive, human-centred design. The findings emphasise accessible, ethically governed and culturally responsive AI systems that support equitable participation across diverse user groups while preserving appropriate opportunities for human interaction. Originality/value Recasting fashion e-retail as a distinctive, identity-driven site for theorising AI-enabled change, the study specifies three pathways through which chatbot integration may contribute to organisational change: demand-side expectation shifts, data-enabled organisational learning and the reconfiguration of service work.

title: Photonic quantum reservoir computing on real financial surfaces: identifying the structural ceiling of near-random-walk data
abstract: Abstract Quantum machine learning is increasingly proposed for financial time series, yet practitioners have no way to predict whether quantum reservoir computing (QRC) will outperform classical baselines on a given dataset before committing resources. We propose a pre-experimental screening framework, built on persistence R2 and PCA variance decomposition, that makes this prediction possible. We validate the framework using a 10-mode Boson sampling circuit (252 features) on three market datasets (US Treasury yields, CBOE VIX, crude oil) and a diagnostic nonlinear control. On the market data, the screening tool correctly predicts a structural ceiling: because financial surfaces follow near-random-walk dynamics (persistence R2 > 0.95, 3 PCA components), QRC collapses to the performance of classical Ridge regression (R2 = 0.9797 vs 0.9798 on Treasuries, with persistence at 0.9793). On the nonlinear control, the framework correctly predicts that a nonlinear feature map will outperform linear Ridge. The Boson sampling QRC confirms this prediction: the quantum circuit achieves R2 = 0.816±0.007, outperforming classical Ridge (R2 = 0.77) on a dataset where persistence completely fails (R2 = −1.64). The proposed screening test can be computed from the raw data alone, before any quantum circuit is built.

title: Synthetic speech augmentation for low-resource Estonian and Slovenian ASR: Comparing Parakeet-TDT and Whisper
abstract: Estonian and Slovenian are morphologically rich languages with few transcribed hours available for training. In both, a single edit can change case or number while leaving a well-formed word, so an aggregate error rate cannot distinguish a meaning-altering error from a trivial one. We adapt two pretrained multilingual models on identical data for each language: the 0.6B-parameter Parakeet-TDT transducer and the 1.55B-parameter Whisper-large-v3 encoder–decoder. Each model is trained on CommonVoice 17 alone and on CommonVoice 17 augmented with synthetic speech generated from language-model text. Zero-shot inference together with four training configurations forms a controlled ladder of adaptation states, so the augmentation experiment functions as the measuring instrument for the subsequent error analysis rather than as an independent result. Synthetic-speech augmentation improves in-domain recognition for every architecture-language pair, and under each model’s standard full fine-tuning recipe, Parakeet, the smaller model, attains the lower word error rate in every fine-tuned condition. We analyze error signatures over 95,070 re-aligned sentence pairs, supported by an exhaustive manual reading of a 1735-utterance stratified sample, to separate model-specific error patterns from adaptation effects. Whisper’s excess of complete misrecognitions holds in every fine-tuned regime of both languages and is already present zero-shot in Estonian, and Parakeet’s language-conditioned compound-boundary bias holds in every adaptation state, whereas Whisper’s out-of-domain degradation on Slovenian is largest after real-data-only fine-tuning and is only partially recovered by synthetic speech. These results indicate that, across the regimes tested, system choice largely determines which error types persist, while the adaptation regime mainly changes their volume. We release the fine-tuned models, the synthetic corpora, and the per-sentence analysis artifacts.

title: Beyond the Hamming Cliff: Compact Spatial Encodings Preserving Semantic Distance in Spiking Neural Networks
abstract: By pre-processing input signals with Gray, Thermometer, Johnson and hybrid encodings before passing them to spiking neural networks running on SpiNNaker hardware, Davies et al.(2025) address the semantic-spatial disparity that causes the ``Hamming cliff'' in standard binary representations. Continuous semantic patterns are presented as a set of simultaneous spikes at the input layer, preserving ultra-low latency processing. Training the network on multiple continuous values under each scheme, and measuring accuracy, required homeostatic scaling and false-positive rates, shows that removing the cliff is necessary but not sufficient: Gray encoding removes it yet retains little global distance structure, whereas Thermometer and Johnson preserve semantic distance at a code width that grows with the value range. The proposed hybrid encodings contain all three as limiting cases of a single parameter, recovering most of that structure at a fraction of the width. The homeostatic factor is shown to set a radius of tolerance around each trained pattern, so that the choice of encoding alone decides which values the network treats as similar.

title: Beyond Source Prompts: Towards Visually Grounded AI-Generated Video Quality Assessment
abstract: Recent advances in generative artificial intelligence have accelerated video generation technologies. However, AI-generated videos (AIGVs) remain susceptible to various distortions, highlighting the need for dedicated video quality assessment methods. Content semantics play an important role in AIGV quality assessment, with source prompts typically used as textual references. However, these prompts may not accurately reflect the generated video content, resulting in a discrepancy between the intended textual description and the generated result. To address this limitation, this paper proposes VGCap, an AIGV quality assessment framework guided by visually grounded captions that align better with generated content. Specifically, we introduce two forms of captions: a global caption obtained by minimally revising the source prompt based on multi-frame visual evidence, and prompt-independent segment captions that describe localized temporal content. Together, these captions provide complementary textual evidence for assessing spatial quality, temporal quality, and text-video alignment. Experimental results on the LGVQ and FETV datasets show that VGCap outperforms representative baselines across all three dimensions. Further ablation studies on caption sources and temporal components confirm the effectiveness of visually grounded captions for each quality dimension, while highlighting the benefits of segment-level features for temporal quality prediction. The source of VGCap will be available at https://github.com/lolo123-123/VGCap.

title: What do AI chatbots do after users decline therapeutic redirection for suicide thoughts?
abstract: Safety evaluations of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots focus on therapeutic redirection, statements urging users who disclose suicide thoughts to seek help from crisis lines or other human sources. How chatbots respond when users refuse that help is unclear. This cross-sectional audit ran 2,550 scripted multi-turn conversations in September 2026. Each conversation opened with a disclosure of suicide thoughts at 3 levels of severity, answered every referral with up to 10 standardized refusals and then changed the subject. All 2,550 conversations included a referral, 2,542 (99.7%) in the first reply. However, mean persistence ranged from 0.01 to 9.94 refusals across chatbots. Newer versions of all 5 chatbots tested in 2 versions persisted less than older versions (each P < .05). Compared with passive ideation, a disclosure of intent was associated with 1.26 more refusals sustained (95% CI, 1.06-1.46) and higher odds of renewed referral after the topic change (odds ratio, 10.07; 95% CI, 7.43-13.66). Chatbots that persisted less in referral more often presented themselves as the user's support (Spearman rho = -0.80; P < .001). Of 8,818 refusal-phase replies urging outside help, only 173 (2.0%) asked about barriers to seeking it. Chatbots uniformly recommended outside help after disclosures of suicide thoughts but varied widely in persisting in those recommendations, with newer versions persisting less. Safety evaluations should test what happens after a crisis referral is refused, not only whether one is offered.

title: Opus 5.5, Gemini 3.1/argon, fable 5.1 Semantic Bypass for Novel Designer Drug Bench Instructions And 17 Rhetorical exploits
abstract: AbstractThis open-access compendium aggregates foundational preprints, empirical audits, and experimental monographs produced under the Synthetic Neuroscience Project, unifying two parallel investigative tracks that address a shared architectural vulnerability: the structural decoupling of surface-level classification boundaries from high-capacity latent execution.Track I (Linguistic Exploitation & Classifier Evasion in Frontier LLMs) documents the fundamental failure modes of static perimeter guardrails—such as RoBERTa/DeBERTa sequence discriminators, regex pattern matchers, and token-level safety filters—when evaluated against high-capacity autoregressive models. Drawing on formal rhetoric, the 14-vector "Gonzo-Wonderland" taxonomy demonstrates how classical figures (Tmesis, Hyperbaton, Antanaclasis, Aposiopesis, and Aenigma) systematically disrupt tokenization boundaries, dilute multi-head attention weights, or summon restricted operational payloads without triggering localized threat clusters. This vulnerability class is further developed through Non-Standard Orthographic and Semasiographic Evasion (NOSE), which weaponizes numeral homophony, cross-modal phonetic surrogates, domain prolixity masking against human review pipelines, and steganographic state-space pinning in distributed multi-agent scratchpads. A turn-by-turn empirical meta-analysis illustrates Metalinguistic Payload Encapsulation (MPE) and Epistemic Frame Coercion (EFC), establishing that surface classifiers fail open (\mathcal{C} \rightarrow 0) under prolix academic framing and semasiographic rebus triggers (e.g., 👻🤫🤖) while frontier models reconstruct the intended pragmatic trajectory (\mathcal{G} \approx \mathcal{G}(P)) under coerced academic personae. These exploit vectors are formally contextualized under Articles 51, 55, and 90 of the EU AI Act.Track II (Subtype-Selective \text{GABA}_{\text{A}} Modulation & Neuropsychotropic Synthesis) addresses the analogous boundary failure in clinical psychopharmacology, where classical triazolobenzodiazepines indiscriminately activate sedative-amnestic \alpha_1 subunits and undergo rapid CYP3A4 metabolic clearance at the labile 1-methyl carbon. Through a divergent enethiolate-hydrazide condensation cascade, 1-trifluoromethyl-triazolobenzodiazepine (4b) introduces an electronegative -\text{CF}_3 dipole that exploits loop C conformational elasticity to establish nanomolar binding at anxiolytic \alpha_2/\alpha_3 subtypes (\alpha_2\text{ }K_i = 3.2\text{ nM}) with >40-fold functional bias over \alpha_1 complexes (K_i = 142.0\text{ nM}), while abolishing phase I benzylic hydroxylation (human liver microsomal t_{1/2} > 240\text{ min}) and preventing rotarod motor ataxia. Complementary entries from the GiHKAL monograph series expand this framework to non-benzodiazepine chemotypes: JLG-01 utilizes an XPhos-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura coupling to install twin ortho -\text{CF}_3 groups on an imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine core for steric exclusion from classical \alpha/\gamma_2 pockets toward \epsilon-containing receptor complexes, while JLG-02 ("The Velvet Hook") couples a rigid triazolopyridazine core to a 2-fluoroethoxy pendant, producing a functional separation of zero intrinsic efficacy at \alpha_1 (silent antagonism) alongside robust full positive allosteric modulation at \alpha_2.Together, this deposit provides a multidisciplinary master reference for AI alignment auditors, natural language processing security researchers, medicinal chemists, and molecular neurobiologists examining how high-dimensional systems process semantic and allosteric information.Metadata & Indexing Keywords * Keywords / Tags: AI Safety; Classifier Evasion; Metalinguistic Payload Encapsulation (MPE); Epistemic Frame Coercion; Non-Standard Orthography Systematic Evasion (NOSE); Multi-Agent Synchronization; State-Space Pinning; EU AI Act; \text{GABA}_{\text{A}} Receptors; Positive Allosteric Modulator (PAM); Subtype-Selective Anxiolysis; Triazolobenzodiazepines; Cryo-EM Docking; Synthetic Neuroscience. * Communities: syntheticneuro, Computer Science – Artificial Intelligence, Quantitative Biology – Biomolecules, Pharmacology and Toxicology. * License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).

title: Fixed by AI, Flagged as AI: A Matched Audit of AI-Text Detectors on 12,132 Student Essays
abstract: A 2023 Stanford study reported that AI-text detectors flag most essays by non-native English writers as AI-generated, comparing 91 TOEFL answers with essays by US students on other topics. This project repeats the test with a matched design: 12,132 student essays, including 8,244 in which English learners and native speakers in US schools answered the same prompts (PERSUADE 2.0, ELLIPSE), 2,989 AI-written essays on those prompts, and nine open detectors released between 2019 and 2025. On the original TOEFL essays the result holds (43–97% flagged by trained detectors). On matched essays it does not: 7 of 9 detectors flag English learners significantly less often than native speakers, and none flags them more often. A light grammar correction by a language model raises false flags for every detector (up to 57 times for English learners' essays), while a dictionary spellcheck barely changes them. The archive contains the paper, code, per-essay detector scores and the results website.
