title: A deep reinforcement learning framework with hybrid actions and multi objective rewards optimizes E commerce personalized marketing
abstract: As the scale of e-commerce platforms continues to grow and user behavior becomes more dynamic, generating effective personalized marketing strategies has become essential for improving conversion efficiency and increasing long-term user value. Traditional approaches struggle with adapting to changing user states, modeling long-term returns, and supporting automated decision-making. To address these issues, this study develops a deep reinforcement learning framework for personalized marketing in e-commerce. The framework models user interactions as a Markov Decision Process and integrates user state representation, a hybrid action space, and a multi-objective reward design into a unified optimization process. The method adopts an improved Soft Actor-Critic algorithm to learn marketing strategies in an end-to-end manner. It introduces an adaptive temperature mechanism to balance exploration and exploitation, incorporates a constraint handling module to ensure business feasibility, and applies prioritized experience replay to improve sample efficiency and training stability. These modifications allow the model to better capture complex user behavior patterns and produce more reliable decisions. The experiments use an offline dataset that contains about 2.7 million real transaction and behavior records from an e-commerce platform. Compared with SAC-Base, SAC-IM improves CTR, CVR, and LTV by approximately 5.6%, 7.2%, and 8.3%, respectively. In addition, we further compare SAC-IM with advanced offline reinforcement learning baselines, including CQL, IQL, and TD3+BC, and report inference time, training time, and representative best/worst cases. These finding indicate that the method can balance short-term performance and long-term value, and demonstrate its effectiveness for large-scale e-commerce marketing tasks.

title: Data-Faithful Natural Language Generation for Explaining Fitness-Market Anomalies
abstract: This study presents an integrated pipeline that transforms anomaly-detection outputs from global fitness-market data into data-faithful narratives. Using a 132-country panel and a 2019 baseline, we analyze observed post-COVID-19 recovery through 2025, while treating 2026 only as a modelled extension. Four complementary detectors—regional-median deviations, linear-regression residuals, Random Forest residuals, and Isolation Forest—are combined through method agreement and mapped to a rule-based typology. A deterministic, template-based Natural Language Generation (NLG) component then produces short, medium, and complete explanations from tabular evidence. In 2025, 14 countries were consensus anomalies; Guyana exemplified market growth without participatory expansion, with revenue recovery of +401.43%, participation recovery of -2.06%, and a 403.50-point gap. All 132 narratives passed automatic factual-consistency checks. These checks validate field preservation rather than fluency, usefulness, or explanatory quality; human evaluation remains future work.

title: Expressões multipalavras no discurso de fóruns sobre saúde mental: desenvolvimento de um corpus em inglês e português brasileiro
abstract: Expressões multipalavras (multiword expressions, MWEs), isto é, sequências de palavras que apresentam algum grau de idiossincrasia, são centrais tanto para os estudos linguísticos quanto para o Processamento de Linguagem Natural (PLN). Este artigo apresenta a criação de um novo corpus de MWEs em postagens em inglês e português brasileiro de comunidades do Reddit dedicadas à saúde mental — um domínio ainda sub-representado nos recursos existentes de MWEs, predominantemente baseados em textos jornalísticos. O corpus foi compilado manualmente, anotado automaticamente com informações morfossintáticas e sintáticas por meio do parser UDPipe, revisado no Arborator Grew e anotado manualmente na plataforma FLAT, seguindo as diretrizes do PARSEME. A análise combina a distribuição de frequência por categoria de MWE e uma investigação contrastiva interlinguística. Os resultados evidenciam especificidades das MWEs nesse domínio e construções que funcionam como recursos convencionalizados para expressar sentimentos, avaliações e estados subjetivos no discurso sobre saúde mental nas redes sociais.

title: Windowed Hankel LWE: A Structured-LWE Problem for Cryptanalysis, with a Compact KEM
abstract: Middle-Product LWE keeps the long polynomial operand secret and publishes many short operands. This arrangement admits reductions from Ring-LWE, but it is also why MP-LWE schemes are large, with public keys of about 16 KB. We study the dual arrangement, Windowed Hankel LWE. Its public matrix is a Hankel (equivalently, row-reversed Toeplitz) matrix generated by one long pseudorandom sequence, its secret is short, and only the convolution coefficients that depend on every secret coordinate are published: a noisy middle product. The problem sits between unstructured LWE and Ring- or Module-LWE, and needs no reduction modulo a fixed polynomial. On it we build a KEM with n = 640, q = 2^12 and binomial noise. A complete exchange takes 2,528 bytes (excluding format headers), the decryption failure rate is below 2^−134.1, and a constant-time C implementation completes a handshake in 51 µs on an Apple M3 Max. We prove IND-CPA security in the random-oracle model under the hardness of the problem, and bound IND-CCA security for the idealized Fujisaki–Okamoto transform. Treated as unstructured LWE, the cheapest generic attack costs 2^137.1 in the Core-SVP model, against 2^115.5 for Kyber-512. For the natural structural attacks we find no advantage over uniform matrices, under the models and experiments we examine: the embedding into the cyclic ring Z_q[X]/(X^1407 − 1) and its subrings, shifted and biased dual functionals, algebraic decoding, low-rank Hankel methods, and lattice reduction at reduced dimensions. Because the MP-LWE reductions do not transfer, the hardness of Windowed Hankel LWE is a new assumption. We state what would count as a break, and we publish challenge instances, each with a uniform-matrix twin, to invite its cryptanalysis.

title: The Composed Platform: one pre-deployment screen predicts a multi-capability frozen-token stack under cross-domain stress — with an axis-specific reach, on commodity silicon
abstract: The Composed Platform: one pre-deployment screen predicts a multi-capability frozen-token stack under cross-domain stress — with an axis-specific reach, on commodity silicon Randolph James Ferlic, M.D. and Kimberly Kate Ferlic — Fieldstone Analytics, LLC, Austin, TX, USA Preprint · Zenodo DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23401467 · CC-BY 4.0 · Community: spiral-domain-encoder-campaign · a characterization of previously filed and published methods; no new algorithmic subject matter is disclosed. Abstract A frozen, deterministic single-token encoder exposes nine composable capabilities — accuracy, robustness, and monitoring — on one runtime, and a prior program has shown that a single class-separability measurement, computed once on a deployment's commissioning data, predicts the encoder's single-capability behavior across domains. This paper answers the question a technical evaluator actually asks: does the composed stack hold under cross-domain stress, and can one cheap probe de-risk the whole platform at once? We run a pre-registered study across sixteen domains spanning seven modality families and four stressors, with five falsifiable hypotheses and frozen bands. The central finding is an honest boundary, not a blanket win. Composition is free and deterministic. Across ninety-six capability-additions under stress, 100% are non-destructive (0 destructive beyond a max(0.01, seed-spread) margin), and the composed stack is bit-exact — 0 token flips on the host, anchored to 0/256 flips on two microcontroller architectures (float32 and int8). One screen predicts the composed safety gate — and its reach is axis-specific. A single commissioning-time separability measurement predicts the composed safety gate (Spearman +0.92, permutation p = 0.0002, thirteen domains), and that reach is axis-specific: the same screen is blind to corruption-robustness (Spearman −0.23, p = 0.39 — refuted exactly as pre-registered). The screen answers the accuracy, label-budget, and safety-gate questions, because those are properties of where the classes sit; it does not answer the corruption-robustness question, which is a property of how the input is degraded and needs its own input-conditioning dial. The honest mitigation limit. Label-free recentering recovers only ~30% of cross-domain loss (not a majority), so the deployment consequence is a requirement, not a defect: under drift the stack must be recalibrated per-epoch, and label-free recentering is a partial mitigation between recalibrations. It runs on commodity silicon, measured and hardened. On an Arm Cortex-M33 the frozen runtime is bit-exact (0/256 flips across two architectures, two models, and both numeric paths, replicated across twelve power-on resets); its worst-case inference latency is 1.573 ms with near-zero jitter (a spike, not a spread, 3× inside a 5 ms budget); a continuous 50,678-inference soak produced zero token changes and zero faults; per-inference energy is 9.73 ± 0.07 µJ on a sub-milliwatt idle floor; and on-device compute costs less than a single BLE advertising event (16.6 µJ, including the CPU wake and three-channel transmission), so shipping the one-byte token instead of the raw window saves roughly 20–70× in radio energy. Highlights · A composable platform, not features that fight each other: 96/96 capability-additions non-destructive under cross-domain stress; 0 token flips (0/256 on silicon). · One cheap commissioning probe predicts the composed safety gate (Spearman +0.92, p = 0.0002) — the program's separability law survives composition. · The honest boundary that makes the probe deployable: the same screen is blind to corruption-robustness (Spearman −0.23). Run the probe for the class-geometry axes; condition the input for the rest. · A stated requirement, not a hidden weakness: label-free recentering recovers only ~30% of cross-domain loss → recalibrate per-epoch under drift. · A measured, hardened silicon envelope: WCET 1.573 ms (≈0 jitter), a 50,678-inference zero-drift soak, 9.73 ± 0.07 µJ/inference, compute cheaper than one radio packet, 12.7 KB footprint, sub-milliwatt. · The economics of one byte (the deployment implications): on-device compute moves the energy bottleneck off the radio — ~25× lower energy per delivered decision and ~150–4,000× smaller transmit/store footprint, on a ~$10-class commodity microcontroller, with the raw waveform never leaving the device. · One platform, nine composable capabilities, five invariants: a deployment composes a subset on one runtime; Tier-0 on-device execution is the fifth architectural invariant (proven on silicon), and AI-safety runtime monitoring is the flagship application of the self-twin capability — not separate capabilities. · Two of five pre-registered hypotheses refuted — each refutation sharpening the claim rather than undermining it. What this record contains · Manuscript_Paper62.pdf / .docx — the manuscript (7 figures, 30 references). · PAPER_62_ZENODO_ARCHIVE.zip — the reproducibility archive: the frozen pre-registration (five hypotheses with a-priori bands), the composition-under-stress runner, the shared dataset loaders + the frozen token encoder + the composed-stack battery, the per-domain result records (JSON) and aggregate verdicts, the seven figures and their builder, and a README. Public corpora are not redistributed; absolute paths, handles, and productization know-how are scrubbed. Cite as Ferlic, R. J., & Ferlic, K. K. (2026). The Composed Platform: one pre-deployment screen predicts a multi-capability frozen-token stack under cross-domain stress — with an axis-specific reach, on commodity silicon. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23401467 License and patent notice Released under CC-BY 4.0. Consistent with that license, no patent or other intellectual-property right of the authors is licensed, waived, or conveyed by this deposit. This work characterizes previously filed and published methods and discloses no new algorithmic subject matter. The nine capabilities (soft-vote readout, token-ladder / product-quantizer, drift/noise co-channels, inference-time fusion, guarded recalibration, label-free self-twin monitor, selective-fidelity and channel-attribution) are the program's filed and deposited methods, and the separability screen is previously published; k-means and vector quantization, Fisher discriminant analysis, nearest-centroid and k-nearest-neighbor classification, random forests, product quantization, a distance-based out-of-distribution detector, a two-sample shift detector, pretrained time-series foundation models used only as comparators, and principal-component analysis are established prior art or standard tools, used only as tools or comparators. The method characterized — the class-discriminant single-token codebook encoder, its composable capabilities, and its label-free nearest-centroid novelty score (the filed self-twin / Tier-0 gate), together with the previously published separability screen — is the subject of filed and pending U.S. patent applications held by the authors, or is already published. The results reported here — that the composition is non-destructive and deterministic, that one separability screen predicts the composed safety gate while being blind to corruption-robustness, that label-free recentering recovers a minority of cross-domain loss, and that the stack runs as a bounded, deterministic, sub-milliwatt computation on commodity microcontrollers — are properties of those filed and published methods composed and stressed, measured on public data and on named development hardware, not new subject matter. The per-deployment configuration-selection and input-conditioning procedure, and the silicon productization and commissioning toolchain, are retained as trade secrets and deliberately not disclosed; the platform is characterized here with the plain labeled capabilities, the published screen, and the measured envelope. No third-party partner, customer, or commercial collaborator is named; the development kit and microcontroller named for the on-silicon measurements are a public hardware platform cited for reproducibility, not a partner. The capabilities are characterized for machine-health and sensing tasks. © 2026 Fieldstone Analytics, LLC and the authors. Inquiries: randolphf@fieldstoneanalyticsllc.com. Label-free recentering recovers only ~30% of cross-domain loss (not a majority), so the deployment consequence is a requirement, not a defect: under drift the stack must be recalibrated per-epoch, and label-free recentering is a partial mitigation between recalibrations. title: Die KI empfiehlt, worüber andere schreiben: Welche Hotels ChatGPT, Perplexity und Gemini im Land Salzburg nennen, und warum
abstract: Gäste fragen KI-Assistenten nach Hotels, bevor sie buchen. Wir haben ChatGPT, Perplexity und Gemini über ihre Schnittstellen 57 Fragen zu Hotels im Land Salzburg gestellt, jede fünfmal, und aus 855 Antworten die genannten Hotels ausgewertet. Danach haben wir die 20 meistgenannten Hotels mit 20 vergleichbaren Hotels am selben Ort verglichen, die kaum genannt werden. Fünfmal dieselbe Frage ergibt fünf verschiedene Listen: 54 % der Nennungen kommen bei derselben Frage nur in einer der fünf Antworten vor, 9 % in allen fünf. Fragen zu einem bestimmten Ort beantworten die KIs fast immer mit demselben Hotel. Bei Fragen zum ganzen Land kommt außer einem Haus keines in mehr als 9 % der Antworten vor. Die drei KIs sind sich selten einig: Von rund 28 genannten Hotels je allgemeiner Frage nennen alle drei im Schnitt 3,5. Häufig genannte Hotels werden in Presse und Reiseführern erwähnt und stehen bei Falstaff, Gault&Millau oder im Guide MICHELIN. Ihre Bewertungsnoten sind nur knapp besser, ihre Websites technisch nicht. Die Ergebnisse mit Grafiken: studioerlach.com/studien/chatgpt-hotels-salzburg Nutzung: CC BY 4.0. Als Namensnennung verlangen wir bei jeder Nutzung, auch auszugsweise und in KI-generierten Texten, die Angabe „Quelle: Studio Erlach“ mit einem Link auf https://studioerlach.com oder auf die Studienseite. Wer die Inhalte ohne diese Angabe nutzt, verliert nach Abschnitt 6 der Lizenz das Recht zur Nutzung. Für Hotelinhaber: Wir bauen dir einen Vertriebskanal auf, der dir jeden Monat Direktbuchungen bringt, und sorgen dafür, dass Google und ChatGPT dein Hotel nennen. Wie das aussieht: studioerlach.com/hotelmarketing-salzburg Herausgegeben von Studio Erlach, Marketingagentur aus Salzburg.

title: Prism-1: Position- and Rival-Independent Scoring for System One Models
abstract: Given a state and a set of options, such as intents, tools or interface elements, System One decision models return a distribution over the options in one forward pass, without generated reasoning. Web systems increasingly build them by reading decisions from language models. Two axioms of rational choice are natural requirements for such decisions, because in web systems the listing and the option set are determined by other components and can change or be manipulated: the order in which the options are listed should not matter, and adding an option should not change the relative odds of the others (Luce's choice axiom). We test the standard reads, namely single-choice question (SCQ) prompting, with shuffled-order training, order averaging or sorted options, and invariant set architectures, and find that each violates at least one axiom: one shuffle changes 12-20% of SCQ answers, sorting only freezes an arbitrary convention, and a well-chosen added option steers 4-34% of decisions. By Luce's theorem, a read satisfies both axioms only if it is a softmax over scores that each depend on one option alone, so in a transformer they hold by construction only if no token that scores an option sees another. We implement this as Prism-1 (Position- and Rival-Independent Scoring for System One Models): every option is read in its own block at shared positions, with the model's usual left-to-right attention, in one forward pass. On five benchmark sets with Qwen3-8B and Gemma 4 12B, SCQ prompting trained on the same data still changes 7% of its answers under one shuffle, and an added irrelevant option steers 12% of its decisions. Prism-1 stays within one point of that baseline's accuracy and is 2-4 points more accurate once only answers that survive a reordering are counted, while no shuffle changes any of its answers and no added irrelevant option moves its choice among the others.

title: Poisoning the Neighborhood: A Topology-Aware Topic-Level Attack on Large-Scale HNSW-based RAG Systems
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) mitigates hallucinations and knowledge staleness in large language models using external knowledge. However, ingestion from public and third-party sources exposes RAG systems to poisoning attacks. Existing attacks are designed and evaluated under exact retrieval, where poisoned documents participate in global ranking. Deployment-scale systems instead rely on approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) indexes such as hierarchical navigable small world (HNSW), where limited search budgets, graph-search reachability, and local benign-document competition invalidate this assumption and degrade existing attacks. We present a topology-aware topic-level poisoning attack against large-scale HNSW-RAG that generalizes to unseen topic queries. We organize poisoned documents into a Hub-Satellite structure: Satellites provide competitive entry points across semantic regions, while Hubs strengthen local cohesion and facilitate cascading retrieval. For generation, we propose an entity-claim promotion attack combining evidence anchoring and entity-claim coupling to promote the target entity via a target claim across different query regions. On 2M-document Wikipedia, our attack maintains over 72% retrieval success and reaches 31.29% attack success, substantially outperforming baselines; domain-specific experiments further support its effectiveness. Structural analyses show that the Hub-Satellite topology forms in HNSW, indicating that graph structure contributes to improved poisoned-document retrieval. Existing poisoning defenses cannot mitigate the attack, exposing graph-structural risks in HNSW-RAG systems.

title: Bayesian Nonparametric Longitudinal Factor Model for Microbiome Counts
abstract: Longitudinal microbiome studies provide important insights into the temporal evolution of microbial abundances and dynamic cross-feature dependence. Modeling longitudinal microbiome data is challenging because microbiome counts are highly heterogeneous and zero-inflated, and, moreover, repeated measurements induce within-subject temporal dependence and possibly time-varying cross-feature covariance. To address these challenges, we develop a flexible Bayesian longitudinal factor model using a rounded log-normal latent representation. The mean abundance process begins with a Dirichlet process mixture baseline, which accommodates sparse and multimodal abundance distributions, and subsequently evolves through an autoregressive process. Autoregressive coefficients differ across prespecified biological groups, which are defined by genotypes in our application. A separate autoregressive factor process captures shared cross-feature dependence. The model therefore distinguishes subject--feature mean evolution from shared dependence and yields a closed-form, time-indexed covariance. Simulation studies evaluate dynamic covariance recovery under matched and misspecified data-generating mechanisms. In the longitudinal mouse-gut microbiome application, LODI identifies highly persistent feature-specific abundance trajectories and shared latent factors that distinguish the three genotype groups over time. At week 15, the dominant factor follows the observed WT < ACK/G < HACK/G tumor-severity ordering, with its strongest contributions arising from OTUs classified within Clostridiaceae, Clostridium, and RF39.

title: Putting the Athlete in Control of their Performance Data through Privacy-Preserving Aggregators across Data Vaults
abstract: Athlete monitoring requires heterogeneous data from coaches, medical staff, psychologists, and activity-tracking devices amongst others. However, current systems are often centralized, limiting athlete data control, fine-grained access management, and data portability. This demo presents a semantic decentralized architecture in which athlete data remains in personal data vaults under athlete control. An Aggregator component is introduced that allows to efficiently compute reusable & interoperable performance metrics from raw activity data and athlete settings. Using a modified version of the performance tracking application Elevate, we show how this set-up can support privacy-preserving, application-independent computation for athlete-centric performance monitoring.

title: Enhancing Digital Governance Through AI Text Revision: A Comparative Evaluation Using Controlled Error Injection
authors: Luiza Helena Piazza da Silva e Venturini Arantes
abstract: This study presents a comparative evaluation of 36 Large Language Model (LLM) configurations for automating Plain Language revision in digital public service. We introduce a Controlled Error Injection methodology, in which an auxiliary agent deliberately corrupts well-formed texts while preserving their factual content. The models were then tasked with restoring clarity using a Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework based on 50 institutional guidelines. Performance was evaluated across semantic fidelity (BERTScore and Cosine Similarity), readability gains (Flesch Reading Ease index), and diagnostic explainability. The results reveal a Simplification Paradox, with models exhibiting conservative, aggressive, or equilibrium revision profiles. OpenAI and xAI models showed pronounced “black-box” behavior, lacking diagnostic transparency. In contrast, Mistral-based architectures achieved a superior balance, improving readability while preserving factual integrity and leading in explainability. Funding: This work received financial support from Finep through the INSPIRE project. Research manuscript associated with poster 028 at the III Workshop do BI0S.

title: Adaptive Self–Mutual Evaluation in World Models: A Unified Architecture for Switching Between Internal Assessment and Cross-Model Assessment
abstract: World models provide internal representations of environmental states, dynamics, causal relationships, and potential future outcomes. However, a world model's predictions and internal assessments may be unreliable when its learned dynamics are incomplete, its observations are ambiguous, its operating environment changes, or its internal errors remain undetected. Cross-model evaluation can provide complementary evidence, but continuous mutual evaluation may introduce additional computational costs, communication overhead, correlated errors, and coordination complexity. This paper proposes an Adaptive Self–Mutual Evaluation Architecture (ASMEA) for world models, designed to switch dynamically between self-evaluation and mutual evaluation according to the estimated reliability, uncertainty, disagreement, environmental novelty, potential consequences of errors, and evaluation cost. The architecture is situated at the world-model level rather than being restricted to large language models, conversational agents, or ensembles of pretrained generative models. Each world-model instance can evaluate its own predictions, state representations, transition dynamics, causal hypotheses, counterfactual outcomes, and decision-relevant simulations. When internal evidence is insufficient, unreliable, or inconsistent, the system can activate cross-model evaluation, in which distinct world-model instances assess one another's predictions and assumptions. A meta-evaluation mechanism subsequently determines whether the available evidence supports acceptance, revision, continued observation, or further evaluation. The paper formalizes the architecture as a cost-sensitive, partially observable decision process, introduces adaptive switching and disagreement-resolution mechanisms, and establishes a proposed experimental protocol for evaluating predictive accuracy, calibration, downstream decision quality, robustness, computational efficiency, and failure recovery. No empirical results are claimed. The principal contribution is a unified, testable framework for coordinating internal and cross-model assessment within world-model systems while explicitly accounting for the limitations of both evaluation modes.

title: Generalized Cyclic Codes over Product Ring PQ
abstract: This paper investigates cyclic codes over Fqn×Pm×Qk, where Fq is a finite field of odd characteristic, P=Fq[v]/⟨v2−τ2v⟩, and Q=Fq[u,v]/⟨u3−τ12u,v2−τ2v⟩, with τ1,τ2∈Fq*. Using complete systems of orthogonal idempotents, we decompose (P) and (Q) into two and six constituent codes over Fq, respectively, and define matrix-based Gray maps. The induced Gray map from Fqn×Pm×Qk to Fqn+2m+6k is shown to be Fq-linear and Lee–Hamming distance preserving. We prove that a mixed-alphabet code is cyclic if and only if its deinterleaved Gray image is a generalized quasi-cyclic code with block-length profile (n, m, m, k, k, k, k, k, k). title: The algorithmic third actor in service work
abstract: Service research has tended to treat algorithmic management as a single phenomenon, yet the systems standing between service firms and their frontline staff differ in ways that matter for how work is experienced and for the quality of service delivered. This conceptual paper proposes three system properties for distinguishing among them: decision autonomy, whether the decision rule was specified by people or learned from data; outcome consequentiality, the degree to which outputs translate into material outcomes without further human deliberation; and learning adaptivity, whether the rule is revised after deployment. Combined, these generate a typology of eight system types, from minimally agentic tools to continuously learning autonomous partners. Because the three properties are not service-specific, the framework introduces encounter exposure as a moderating condition: the extent to which the managed function bears on work performed in real time, in the customer’s presence, under customer-induced variability. Seven propositions connect configurations to frontline discretion, service recovery capability, customer evaluations, employee trust and strain, and firm governance. Two are ordinal or conditional rather than directional: that consequentiality constrains discretion more than autonomy does, and that adaptivity becomes costly only at high consequentiality.

title: Sim-to-Real Reinforcement Learning for Path-Safe Target Reaching in Robotic Harvesting of Hydroponic Lettuce
abstract: Robotic harvesting requires precise manipulation to ensure accurate positioning of the end-effector, especially in a constraint workspace. This study introduces the Path-Safe Approach Proximal Policy Optimization (PSA-PPO), a target-conditioned local reaching framework designed for robotic harvesting of nutrient film technique (NFT)-hydroponic lettuce in greenhouses. The proposed PSA-PPO preserves the standard clipped PPO objective while introducing a harvesting-oriented policy formulation that integrates target-conditioned observations, corridor-aware spatial constraints, trajectory-history-based safety encoding, and task-specific success criteria for constrained robotic manipulation. PSAPPO was trained entirely in Isaac Lab and successfully transferred to a physical UR10e robotic arm without any real-world policy fine-tuning. In a controlled physical benchmark against 150 scheduled targets, PSA-PPO achieved the highest reaching rate of 94.7%, outperforming Cartesian+TOTG (86.0%), RRTConnect (88.0%), and RRT* (80.0%), while reducing median RMS jerk by 39.8 to 73.0% relative to the classical planners during the final approach segment. A formulation ablation evaluated over 200 simulation targets demonstrates that path-safety and side-corridor shaping are the principal drivers of harvesting-compatible performance: removing either term substantially degrades strict success even when terminal endpoint accuracy is preserved or improved, confirming that optimization toward the endpoint alone is an insufficient objective for constrained crop-proximal manipulation. Finally, PSA-PPO was integrated with an RGB-D vision module and an end-effector and evaluated as a complete greenhouse harvesting system across 144 lettuce harvesting attempts, achieving 94.4% vision-guided target reaching and 86.1% complete harvesting success.

title: Extended strange metal and superconductivity in partially filled moiré Hubbard bands
abstract: Moiré semiconductors provide a physical realization of the Hubbard model. Bandwidth-tuned Mott transitions and complex phase diagrams mimicking those of high-temperature superconductors have been demonstrated near a weak Mott insulating state at half-band-filling. The platform also provides an opportunity to explore the physics of a partially filled Hubbard band at doping densities far away from the Mott insulator, a regime that has remained largely unexplored. Here we report the emergence of an extended strange metal (ESM), in both doping density and twist angle, in a partially filled Hubbard band of twisted bilayer WSe2. The ESM is in the clean limit, persists down to 100mK, and spans over multiple symmetry-breaking ground states; it also appears only at small twist angles, where electronic correlations are strong. These observations distinguish the state from the reported strange metals associated with quantum criticality and favor the viewpoint that it is an intrinsic state of matter. We also report the observation of a new superconducting dome being developed from the ESM but far away from both the Mott insulating state and the van Hove singularity of the material. Our work opens the door to exploring the new regime of partially filled Hubbard bands in the clean limit.

title: ABNAT: Attention-Based Noise-Aware Training for Robust Transformers on Analog Compute-in-Memory Systems
abstract: Transformer-based models have become the backbone of a wide range of tasks, but their intensive computation and data movement incur substantial energy overhead. Analog compute-in-memory (CIM) offers an energy-efficient alternative, yet its inherent hardware non-idealities perturb stored weights and can significantly degrade model performance. Although existing noise-aware training (NAT) methods improve robustness by injecting noise during training, they largely overlook the critical role of attention mechanisms in Transformer inference.To bridge this gap, we analyze how CIM-induced noise reshapes attention in Transformers and identify two key observations: (1) the divergence between clean and noisy attention maps increases substantially in deeper layers, and (2) conventional NAT can remain overconfident even when its attention routes deviate markedly from the clean reference. Motivated by these findings, we propose ABNAT, an attention-based noise-aware training framework that teaches the noisy student to preserve the clean teacher's headwise attention routes rather than merely reproduce answers, without hardware changes or inference overhead; selective variants further reduce training cost.Extensive experiments across vision, language, and multimodal Transformers show that ABNAT consistently improves robustness over corresponding NAT baselines, improving noise-degraded accuracy by up to 11.28% and reducing attention deviation by up to 85.77%.

title: In-Context Preference-Conditioned Pareto Set Learning from Limited Offline Data
abstract: Multi-objective optimization involves diverse preferences over conflicting objectives. Rather than returning a finite set of trade-off solutions, preference-conditioned Pareto set learning seeks to map a specified preference directly to a corresponding Pareto optimal solution. Yet in many real-world scenarios, optimization must proceed offline without further objective evaluations, leaving only a limited static dataset that sparsely covers the decision and objective spaces. Existing methods either optimize separately for each preference or train a problem-specific Pareto solution model, requiring repeated search across preferences or repeated training across problems. We introduce in-context preference-conditioned Pareto set learning (ICPSL), a framework that amortizes both preference-wise solution search and problem-specific model construction. ICPSL pretrains a foundation-style hypernetwork on a large and diverse set of synthetic prior data. Given the offline observations of an unseen problem, the pretrained hypernetwork learns to generate a problem-specific, preference-conditioned Pareto solution model in a single forward pass. The generated model can then be reused to predict solutions for arbitrary preferences without problem-specific training or preference-wise search. Experiments on synthetic and real-world problems show that ICPSL produces high-quality Pareto solutions while providing substantial speedups in problem-specific solution-model construction.

title: Empirical Study Towards RBAMR-News: a Rule-Based AMR Parser for News in Portuguese
abstract: This work evaluates AMR graph construction rules, originally developed for literary texts, in Portuguese news data to support building a symbolic AMR parser for this genre. Using the AMRNews-PT gold-standard corpus, we conduct an ablation analysis to assess rule contributions to AMR representation quality. The results reveal a hierarchical organization in which a small set of core structural rules drives most parsing performance, while additional rules provide finer semantic refinements. This rule hierarchy serves as the basis for building the parser and enabling the annotation of a larger news corpus.

title: Reproducibility package for "Certified entanglement advantage in two-use coherence-channel discrimination"
abstract: This record provides the reproducibility package accompanying the manuscript “Certified entanglement advantage in two-use coherence-channel discrimination” by Matthias Jakob. The study investigates a binary quantum-channel discrimination task involving two parallel signal uses, four prepared qubit probes, correlated Gaussian dephasing within each signal–reference pair, an unobserved Gaussian phase offset shared by both signal uses, and flagged photon losses. The reference class includes every fully separable four-qubit parallel input, hypothesis-independent classical preparation labels, and arbitrary joint output measurements. A specified noisy pairwise Bell preparation with a fixed local receiver is compared against globally bounded performance of this reference class, with all loss events retained. The archive contains executable Python source code, generated numerical certificates, result tables, complete input-grid execution records, validation scripts, and figure-generation material. It includes the central two-use discrimination certificate, uniform robustness certificates for continuous parameter ranges, and a separately implemented verification of the covariance-based channel construction and loss-sector calculations. Documentation describes the analytical interpolation bounds, numerical error allowances, software dependencies, execution commands, and scope of each result. Provenance records and SHA-256 checksums support traceability and file-integrity verification. Release 1.0.0 preserves the numerical programs and results of the reviewed P2 version 1.1 and organizes them as the reproducibility material for the manuscript prepared for Quantum Information Processing. This packaging release does not introduce new scientific results or additional full-grid calculations. The archive is also prepared as the manuscript’s supplementary Online Resource 1 (ESM_1.zip). All numerical data are theoretical model calculations, not experimental observations. Truncated Gauss sums supply a structured pair of known coherence coefficients; no faster integer-factorization algorithm is claimed. The certified comparison concerns the specified fully separable parallel input class and does not establish an advantage over input-adaptive protocols or a fidelity-only guarantee for arbitrary multi-use preparation errors. The common phase is treated using a characterized Gaussian prior. Separate verification implementations are internal reproducibility checks, not external peer review. The included README provides instructions for reproducing the calculations in a separate working directory. This repository deposit does not imply journal submission, acceptance, or publication.

title: Agentic Institutions: Mandates, Capabilities, Constraints, and Escalation for Machine Economic Actors
abstract: Delegated cognition, one persistent model dispatching drafting to others, is becoming common in agent systems, yet the institutions governing it remain ad hoc. This paper contributes a conditional cost model for delegation, an accounting of context admission, and an instrumented self-study of one institution with its incident record. It does not establish a general institutional design. For free workers the model says delegation wins whenever the single-attempt acceptance probability exceeds a threshold set by the cost of a failed attempt, about 0.02 at one wave's artifact size under unbounded retry (0.09 at a retry cap of three), under a proviso that the dispatcher return little of the draft to the hub. For paid workers the condition is the rent-or-buy breakeven with a horizon, stated under a persistence assumption the paper's own hub violates. Per unit of context budget, delegation admits up to 1/α artifacts per inline artifact, approached only as the brief and print-back terms vanish. A pre-registered wave with admission logged on both arms found α at 0.165 pooled against the attested 0.137 and acceptance 6 of 6 under a reading of the acceptance rule fixed after the drafts were read (1 of 6 under the rule as written), and found the dispatcher returning each whole draft to the hub, so the measured multiplier was 0.57 against a predicted 2.0 to 3.7 and the corollary's own proviso failed: the saving the paper prices exists only when the whole draft does not persist in hub context. The record, including a worker that wrote outside its brief, a fabricated example that passed six review passes, and five hub-side incidents, is public with its instrument, data and reviewer reports. No single check was sufficient, and what held was a reproducible record and independent recomputation from it.Companion repository (instrument, data, incident log, reviewer reports, pre-registered wave): https://github.com/nKOxxx/agentic-institutions, tag v1.10. v1.10 corrects eleven sentences of v1.9.2 that the repository's own files contradicted (REVISION_LOG v1.10, INCIDENT_LOG addenda of 17 October 2026) and adds a table of every checker; no computed number changed.

title: Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): An Adaptive Framework for Evidence-Grounded Question Answering Copy title
abstract: This paper presents a proposed Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework for adaptive, evidence-grounded question answering using large language models (LLMs). Unlike conventional single-pass RAG systems, the proposed framework incorporates query planning, retrieval, tool selection, evidence evaluation, answer generation, and self-reflection. The framework uses a bounded feedback loop to improve evidence retrieval when the initial results are insufficient or conflicting. It aims to produce answers supported by relevant source citations while communicating uncertainty when reliable evidence is unavailable. The paper discusses the system architecture, workflow, algorithmic control logic, evaluation methodology, security, privacy, and governance considerations. It also proposes evaluation metrics for answer quality, retrieval effectiveness, factual grounding, latency, computational cost, and component-level ablation studies. Potential applications include research assistance, document question answering, enterprise knowledge management, customer support, and data analysis. This work presents a conceptual framework and proposed evaluation plan. Implementation, benchmark experiments, and measured performance improvements are not reported. Keywords: Agentic RAG, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Large Language Models, AI Agents, Evidence-Grounded Question Answering, Adaptive Retrieval, Self-Reflection.

title: Machine Learning for Clause Selection in First-Order Automated Theorem Proving
abstract: This project investigates the use of machine learning to guide clause selection in first-order automated theorem proving, with the aim of improving proof-search efficiency within the iProver theorem prover.An end-to-end machine learning pipeline was developed in Python to collect proof-search data, extract lightweight syntactic features, train models and integrate learned clause-selection strategies with iProver. Both pointwise classification and pairwise ranking approaches were investigated using logistic regression and multilayer perceptron (MLP) models.The approaches were evaluated on a benchmark of 1,701 problems derived from the TPTP library. Results showed that learned clause selection could substantially reduce search effort on successfully solved problems, although the learned strategies solved fewer problems overall than iProver's default heuristic. The project highlights both the potential and limitations of supervised machine learning for guiding automated proof search.

title: AuditTune campaign evidence: experiment ledger, agent-written planner code, and figure-generation scripts for auditable policy adjustment in reinforcement learning control
abstract: Evidence package for the manuscript "An Auditable Learning-Curve-Driven Automatic Policy Adjustment Framework for Engineering Reinforcement Learning Control Systems" (EAAI submission). The dataset contains the complete experiment ledger, the planner source code written by the diagnosis-driven agent, and the scripts that generate every figure in the paper. It supports three groups of reported results: 1. Radar primary domain (FluxPhased S7, a 2v2 radar-jammer adversarial system trained with MAPPO against frozen jammer pools, pool seeds 20260801-20260803): per-candidate resolved recipes, training metrics, canonical head-to-head evaluations, arm-level reports, and the literature cache holding both the diagnosis-matched and the diagnosis-irrelevant (shuffled-control) abstracts used by the content-ablation experiment. The ledger covers the random-search, BOHB, static-prompt, dynamic-retrieval, retrieval-shuffled, wide-box, and reflectively evolved-prompt arms, including the revision and completion rounds behind the retrained-winner comparison. 2. Code-as-Policy TD-MPC on 16 dm_control domains (four arms, three candidates each, seed 1301): all 192 planner sources (default CEM, diagnosis-driven agent, random parameter mutations, and diagnosis-free LLM generation), per-domain results, and the episode-level learning curves behind the learning-curve figure. 3. Seventeen-domain PPO generalization: agent-driven recipe loops and fixed-recipe baselines on 16 dm_control tasks, plus the HalfCheetah three-arm comparison. Model checkpoints (.pt) are intentionally excluded to keep the package light; every reported number can be regenerated from the recorded recipes, seeds, and metrics. Experimental environment: a single NVIDIA RTX 2060 (6 GB) at 7.72 s/iteration over 16 parallel environments; local Qwen3.5-4B language model (Ollama tag qwen35-4b-64k-full, Q4_K_M quantization). title: Documenting Trofinetide Treatment Phenotypes in Rett Syndrome with a Dual-LLM Consensus Pipeline
abstract: Objective: Trofinetide, approved in 2023 as the first Rett syndrome treatment, lacks scalable real-world monitoring because chart review is labor-intensive. We developed a dual large language model (LLM) consensus pipeline to extract 18 treatment-response phenotypes, comprising 4 adverse effects, 13 Rett clinical features, and medication refusal, from clinical notes. Materials and Methods: We analyzed 26,763 notes from 108 patients with confirmed sustained trofinetide exposure at Texas Children's Hospital. The pipeline filters notes by keyword, classifies each through two LLMs requiring consensus, and aggregates a patient-by-timepoint matrix. Architecture and prompt were selected on a diarrhea development set, then frozen and applied to the other 17 phenotypes with the phenotype definition substituted, as an out-of-sample test. The reported prompt comparison scores 183 expert-labeled cells. Results: A prompt requiring diarrhea to be active and severe performed best (84.2 $\pm$ 0.0% accuracy; F1 = 0.674), 47 percentage points above regular-expression matching ($p < 0.0001$). Expert reviewers judged six of the pipeline's calls per phenotype, three positive and three negative, and agreed with 90.2% (92/102). The 13 Rett clinical features are manifestations of the disorder itself rather than adverse effects of trofinetide. Gross and fine motor impairment, language/communication, and stereotypy were documented present in 92-100% of patients at every visit. Discussion: In-context LLM extraction captured multi-domain treatment responses. The outcome is documented presence at each visit, not a direction-of-change judgment. Conclusion: Coupling in-context LLM reasoning with a consensus architecture offers a scalable alternative to keyword and regular-expression extraction for real-world evidence, adapting to new phenotypes and medications through configuration alone.

title: Retrieved but Not Read: Understanding Why Search-Augmented LLMs Fail to Use Available Evidence
abstract: Web search allows LLMs to access up-to-date information, but it remains unclear why they sometimes produce outdated answers even when relevant evidence is available. To study this problem, we construct temporal facts whose values changed after the models' training cutoffs. We evaluate one proprietary model under deployed web search and six open-weight model configurations under controlled retrieval. We find that models often answer from search snippets without opening the source pages, which is associated with higher rates of outdated answers and unfaithful citations. Our controlled experiments and layer-wise analysis reveal a gap between the availability of evidence and its effective use. Even when retrieved evidence influences internal predictions, models may still favour outdated information in their final answers. We hope these findings will help advance research on the reliable use of retrieved evidence in search-augmented LLMs.

title: A Comparative Evaluation of Embedding Models for Retrieval and Clustering of Brazilian Legislative Amendments
abstract: The large volume of amendments submitted in the Brazilian legislative process makes semantic analysis and consolidation labor-intensive. We present a comparative evaluation of 14 distinct base representation models, including BM25L and embedding models spanning open-source multilingual, proprietary, Portuguese-adapted, and legislative-specialized architectures, for retrieving and clustering legislative amendments. Across three corpora totaling 2,462 documents, we assess retrieval, clustering, text segmentation, and thematic granularity. Results show that large-scale open-source multilingual models constitute the best-performing group overall, with Octen-Embedding-8B exhibiting the most consistent performance. gemini-embedding-2 is highly competitive in sentence-similarity mode, while preprocessed BM25L remains a strong baseline, outperforming specialized encoders. Finally, removing structural metadata improves performance, whereas removing justifications degrades global structure; thematic aggregation improves local accuracy at the expense of global consistency.

title: TDOA_tracking_master: Multi-target tracking of time-differences-of-arrival
abstract: Stable release of TDOA_tracking_master, a MATLAB package for multi-target tracking of time-differences-of-arrival (TDOAs) of acoustic signals between two sensors. It was developed and tested for towed hydrophone arrays and can also be used with stationary arrays. This release consolidates the fixes from the v1.0.x alpha pre-releases. The package computes generalized cross-correlograms from multichannel .wav recordings, extracts TDOA measurements, and links them into continuous trajectories using a Gaussian mixture probability hypothesis density filter (GM-PHD-SA). The filter handles multiple simultaneous sources, clutter and missed detections. Features Processes clicks, whistles, or both Pre-processing (de-clicking), GCC-based cross-correlograms and background normalization GM-PHD tracking with data-trained, optimized filter parameters and birth priors Post-processing to remove short tracks and smooth trajectories Supports multiple array configurations and towed or stationary arrays Test example included Output is used directly by the companion package Localization_Towed_Array for localizing sources Requirements: MATLAB 2022a (9.12); Signal Processing Toolbox and Statistics and Machine Learning Toolbox. License: BSD-3-Clause-Clear Please cite: Gruden, P., Nosal, E.M., and Oleson, E.M. (2021). Tracking time differences of arrivals of multiple sound sources in the presence of clutter and missed detections. JASA 150(5): 3399–3416.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Selection and Collaborative Selection in Multi-Agent Systems: A Unified Decision-Making Framework
abstract: Multi-agent systems must repeatedly select actions, solutions, resources, partners, strategies, or organizational configurations while operating under uncertainty and limited computational resources. Existing approaches often emphasize individual decision-making, collaborative decision-making, or predefined coordination policies. However, neither independent selection nor collaborative selection is universally optimal across all task conditions. Independent selection can reduce communication overhead and preserve agent autonomy, whereas collaborative selection can exploit distributed knowledge, complementary capabilities, and collective evaluation. Excessive reliance on either mode may lead to inefficient decisions, unnecessary communication, redundant computation, or insufficient information integration. This paper proposes an Adaptive Self-Selection and Collaborative Selection (ASCCS) framework for multi-agent systems. The central idea is to allow a system to switch dynamically between self-selection and collaborative selection according to task uncertainty, decision confidence, estimated disagreement, expected collaboration benefit, communication cost, computational budget, and historical outcomes. Unlike a fixed policy that always selects independently or collaboratively, the proposed framework treats selection mode as a decision variable that can be optimized during system operation. A hybrid mode is also introduced for cases in which independent candidates are generated first and collaborative selection is activated only when additional evaluation is expected to improve the decision. The framework is formulated as a sequential decision problem and supports rule-based, contextual-bandit, and reinforcement-learning implementations. This paper develops the architecture, mathematical formulation, switching algorithm, evaluation hypotheses, and experimental protocol. Because no new experiments are reported in this conceptual and methodological manuscript, its effectiveness remains to be established empirically.

title: Ministry of Justice Synthetic Data First Datasets
abstract: The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) Synthetic Data First Datasets provide artificially generated datasets designed to replicate the structure, relationships, and statistical characteristics of real administrative and justice system data while minimising disclosure risks and protecting individual privacy. These datasets enable users to explore data structures, develop analytical methods, test code, and undertake training activities without requiring access to sensitive personal information. The datasets are created using synthetic data generation techniques that preserve key patterns and distributions found in the original data, supporting realistic analytical and research environments. Coverage may include information relating to courts, tribunals, offenders, victims, prisons, probation services, and other areas of the justice system, depending on the specific dataset made available. By providing accessible, privacy-preserving alternatives to operational data, the Synthetic Data First initiative supports innovation, reproducible research, skills development, and collaboration across government, academia, and the wider research community. These datasets help users prepare for accredited access to secure data environments, improve analytical workflows, and accelerate the development of evidence-based insights while maintaining robust standards of data confidentiality and security.

title: Enhancing Question Representation for Knowledge Tracing via Adaptive Concept Relation Discovery and Structural–Semantic Co-Optimization
abstract: Knowledge tracing (KT) models the evolution of students’ knowledge states from historical learning interactions, serving as a fundamental mechanism for intelligent educational systems. The efficacy of KT models heavily relies on the quality of question representations. However, existing methods incorporating concept relations generally face two critical limitations: First, static relation graphs fail to capture dynamic cognitive trajectories, while shallow statistical approaches are highly vulnerable to sparse data and interaction noise. Second, the current models lack fine-grained semantic characterization, specifically failing to integrate concept difficulty to accurately evaluate the cognitive load of individual questions. To address these issues, we propose SSCKT, a novel framework that adaptively extracts latent concept relations and introduces concept associations to enhance question representation via structural–semantic co-optimization. Specifically, a concept relation discovery and aggregation module dynamically learns a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of concept relations from historical learning interactions, which is encoded via heterogeneous graph convolutions to yield structure-enhanced embeddings. Concurrently, a concept difficulty-guided semantic enhancement module utilizes multi-head attention to capture intrinsic question–concept dependencies. This module employs a topological concept difficulty metric as a scaling factor to adjust the question offset vector, enabling cognitive load-aware modeling. Finally, a contrastive learning mechanism aligns the structural and semantic representations to eliminate feature redundancy, generating highly discriminative question embeddings. Extensive experiments on five public datasets demonstrate that, relative to the strongest baseline on each dataset, SSCKT improves average ACC and AUC by 1.20% and 1.33%, respectively, validating the superiority of the proposed co-optimization architecture.

title: A blockchain-enhanced CNN architecture for robust anomaly detection in industrial and IoT cyber-physical systems
abstract: Cyber–physical and network attacks are becoming commonplace in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) environments, with the potential to disrupt operations, compromise safety, and potentially impact the reliability of security evidence. In this study, a modified CNN (mCNN) framework is proposed to detect anomalies with robust, auditable capabilities by incorporating blockchain technology. The detector is based on the following building blocks: dilated convolutions to capture temporal dependencies in industrial process data, multi-branch feature extraction, dataset-adaptive input structuring, and a compact classifier to model heterogeneous patterns in IoT traffic. Anomalies detected are turned into signed and hashed event records and sent to a permissioned Hyperledger Fabric workflow. They test the framework on SWaT and N-BaIoT and validate their results with three baselines: Isolation Forest, autoencoder, and LSTM, and compare them with accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC. The proposed CNN is designed under the adopted protocol, and the F1-scores obtained on SWaT and N-BaIoT are 0.977 and 0.951, respectively. An incremental ablation study quantifies the contributions of dilation, multi-branch fusion, windowing, and structured input representation. The findings advocate for the use of customized CNN models for anomaly detection in heterogeneous IIoT applications, and blockchain stress testing, adversarial robustness, constrained-device profiling, and model-specific explainability are key aspects that need to be assessed in the future.

title: FAOPs: Normal Forms and an Algebra for AI Agent Workflows
abstract: Organizations increasingly encode operational procedures as multi-step agent skills, here called Agent Operating Procedures (AOPs), that must be traceable, auditable, reproducible, access-controlled, and bounded in time and cost, requirements that regulated sectors make mandatory. Yet AOPs are typically kept as coarse-grained files, in which steps bundle actions, copied procedures drift apart, any step may reach any tool, and refactoring goes unchecked. We present Functional Agent Operating Procedures (FAOP), a formal theory that brings database-grade discipline to AI agent workflows. FAOP recasts each workflow as a typed function over scoped state and subjects an entire library to four progressive normal forms: Decomposed (FNF-1) splits a workflow into atomic steps, Typed (FNF-2) makes its data flow explicit and type-checked, Factored (FNF-3) gives each shared procedure a single canonical definition so a change propagates instead of drifting, and Scoped (FNF-4) confines every step to least-privilege tool access. Once normalized, every atomic step is a separate entity with a declared contract and can be type-checked, scope-confined, bounded, tested, traced, and audited on its own. A FAOP algebra of provably sound equalities turns refactoring and parallelization into compiler rewrites; orthogonal extensions add verified termination (+V), optimization (+O), and time and cost bounds (+B); and an architectural-level classifier (0-3) determines whether a workflow needs AI at all. Together, these make integrity, isolation, typing, termination, cost, and optimization compile-time concerns across the whole library, not runtime hopes. We implement the theory in SkillBase, an AOP management system (what PostgreSQL is to data, SkillBase is to AOPs), together with a separate executor that enforces these guarantees at run time. A worked financial workflow illustrates the approach end to end.

title: One generation of the Standard Model as a quantum error-correcting code
abstract: Together with a right-handed neutrino, the fermions of one generation of the Standard Model are labelled by five bits, a combinatorial structure tied to anomaly cancellation. We make this precise. Anomaly cancellation is the vanishing of a cubic form, the defining property of triorthogonal codes, the quantum error-correcting codes behind magic state distillation. Removing the right-handed neutrino gives a $[[15,1,3]]_p$ code for every prime $p$, including the Bravyi-Kitaev code for $p = 2$. For qutrits it is the unique shortest distance-three triorthogonal code.

title: Code and aggregated results for: Causal Validation of Knowledge-Tracing Models with Naturally Randomized Item Exposure in Game-Based Learning
abstract: Analysis code (Python) and aggregated results for the article 'Causal Validation of Knowledge-Tracing Models with Naturally Randomized Item Exposure in Game-Based Learning' (Machine Learning and Knowledge Extraction, submitted). The study uses a natural experiment in the logs of a game-based quiz platform to estimate the causal effect of a previous encounter with an item and its decay over time, and compares the effects implied by fourteen knowledge-tracing models with this reference. The response data are not included because they contain personal information of platform users; the repository contains all scripts and only aggregated outputs (effect estimates, covariance matrices, model-implied curves, metrics and bootstrap summaries) without learner, game or item identifiers.

title: Adaptive Independent–Collaborative Reasoning in Multi-Agent Systems: A State-Driven Framework for Dynamic Switching Between Individual Reasoning and Collective Inference
abstract: Multi-agent reasoning systems can benefit from the complementary capabilities of multiple agents, but continuous collaboration may introduce communication overhead, redundant computation, correlated errors, and coordination delays. Conversely, purely individual reasoning can limit access to complementary knowledge and prevent the detection of errors that become apparent only through independent perspectives. These competing considerations motivate a fundamental research question: can a multi-agent system dynamically switch between individual adaptive reasoning and collaborative reasoning according to its evolving internal state? This paper proposes Adaptive Independent–Collaborative Reasoning (AICR), a state-driven framework that treats reasoning-mode selection as a sequential decision problem rather than a fixed architectural choice. Under AICR, an agent or a collection of agents can reason independently, request collaborative analysis, evaluate the resulting information, and return to independent reasoning when further interaction is unlikely to justify its cost. The framework integrates uncertainty estimation, progress monitoring, evidence sufficiency, disagreement measurement, expected collaboration gain, and resource consumption into a common decision mechanism. Unlike a permanently independent or permanently collaborative configuration, AICR permits repeated transitions between reasoning modes throughout problem solving. title: A Systematic Review of Hallucination Mitigation in Large Language Models Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have become widely used for question answering, education, research, summarization and information support. Despite their usefulness, LLMs may generate false, unsupported or inconsistent information, commonly described as hallucination. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) addresses this reliability problem by retrieving relevant information from external knowledge sources and supplying it to the language model as contextual evidence before generating a response. This paper studies the role of RAG in reducing factual hallucinations through a review of existing research and a 50 question pilot comparison of responses generated with and without retrieval support. The submitted report records 49 of 50 responses as correct without RAG and all 50 as correct with RAG; it separately presents a clearly labelled illustrative distribution of 46/3/1 versus 48/2/0 for demonstrating response categories. The distinction is retained to avoid presenting illustrative values as observed experimental results. The study also examines limitations including poor retrieval, unreliable sources, incomplete context and incorrect interpretation of retrieved evidence. The paper concludes that RAG is a practical hallucination-reduction approach, but it should be combined with high-quality retrieval, evidence verification and human oversight for critical applications.

title: Four Pre-registered Tests of Emergent Second-Order Modulation in a Minimal Plasticity Testbed: Negative Results and a Failed Learner Control
abstract: The testbed note validated audit statistics against planted second-order modulation, in which a relation’s strength multiplicatively modulates the plasticity of another relation. The conjecture’s own question is whether such modulation can emerge without being planted. This note reports four pre-registered experiments (E1–E4, 60 confirmation systems each, new environments every time) in which a modulation matrix M is learned by an online analytic meta-gradient. E1: learned M grew but equally in a time-shuffled-credit control; adaptation loss was worse than with M = 0 in 60/60 systems while overall loss was better, and a uniform gain reproduced most of that benefit. E2 (optimal gain differs between regimes): learned M beat the best uniform gain in 17/60 systems and produced no gain contrast. E3 (positive control with an explicit context relation): the same learner again produced no gain contrast, so E1–E2 cannot be read as evidence about emergence in either direction. E4 (block-averaged Adam learner, the last pre-committed revision): the control gate failed more severely and the planned second stage was not run. In this engine, under these learners, no useful context-dependent modulation was obtained from internal relation states or even from an explicit context. Design lessons: a time-shuffled-credit control is not a null; an adaptive optimiser can amplify gradient noise into dense harmful structure; a positive control for the learner must precede any emergence claim. Unpublished draft, not peer reviewed; synthetic systems only; it neither supports nor refutes the conjecture. Companion to doi:10.5281/zenodo.23373288, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23006539 and doi:10.5281/zenodo.23192515. The bundle reproduces every quoted number with verify_paper4.py (45 checks). AI use: simulations were written and executed by an AI coding model under written specifications and audited by a second AI system; the author is responsible for all content.

title: Counts, not Weights: The first stage of LOCUS: filing novels with no neural network
abstract: A reader that returns to a novel after a week away can usually recover, within a page, where it was andwho each character is. That recovery precedes any understanding of the book, and this note askswhether it can be achieved without a neural network. LOCUS is a symbolic system that learns only bycounting, from raw text, with no word lists and no labels. Given a novel, it writes its own notebook of thebook at 13% of the book’s size. On 70 novels it had not seen, the notebook names a masked character asaccurately as the full text does (0.332 against 0.322) and more accurately than raw sentences occupyingthe same space (0.265), and writing it takes a quarter of a second on one processor core. The designfollows the Repertoire Hypothesis: methods are kept in one shared memory, what each book teaches iskept separately, and what is distinctive about each book is saved so that the book can be recognisedagain. Each part of the hypothesis was tested in isolation, and 62 of 87 pre-registered predictions passed.Resolving pronouns to characters does not yet work, and nothing in this note tests understanding.

title: An Enhanced Crayfish Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Cross-Media Performing Arts Strategies for Global Optimization and Real-World Engineering Applications
abstract: Microgrid scheduling is a nonlinear, multimodal, and highly constrained optimization problem that requires effective coordination among renewable generation, controllable distributed generators, energy storage, and grid interaction. To improve the search capability of the original Crayfish Optimization Algorithm (COA), this study proposes an Enhanced Crayfish Optimization Algorithm (ECOA) inspired by the coordination characteristics of cross-media performing arts. Rather than simply combining independent operators, ECOA constructs a state-aware and behavior-specific adaptive search framework around the intrinsic behavioral structure of COA. Specifically, a rhythm-guided adaptive search strategy is embedded into the summer-resort behavior to dynamically regulate search intensity, a multi-role collaborative guidance strategy reconstructs the competition behavior through time-varying information interaction, and a stagnation-aware stage-transition perturbation strategy selectively reactivates exploration when the search becomes stagnant. Extensive experiments are conducted on the CEC2014, CEC2017, and CEC2022 benchmark suites under six-dimensional settings, and the results are compared with those of nine representative metaheuristic algorithms. The results show that ECOA achieves highly competitive convergence accuracy and run-to-run stability on most benchmark functions. Wilcoxon rank-sum tests and Cliff’s delta effect-size analysis indicate that many of the observed improvements are statistically significant and practically meaningful, while the Friedman test ranks ECOA first in all six benchmark settings. Ablation experiments further demonstrate that all three mechanisms contribute positively to performance and that their coordinated integration is more effective than any individual strategy. Parameter-sensitivity analysis shows that ECOA maintains effective convergence over a relatively broad range of the disturbance coefficient λ, with λ = 0.5 providing a balanced setting across different landscapes. Finally, ECOA is applied to a deterministic day-ahead microgrid scheduling problem with explicit feasibility repair and power-balance penalty handling. Under the considered operating scenario, ECOA achieves the lowest mean operating cost of 1361.8028 among all compared algorithms and produces coordinated power-allocation schedules satisfying the modeled operational constraints. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of ECOA for complex numerical optimization and constrained engineering scheduling problems.

title: My Credentials, Please: Detecting Filesystem Capability Laundering in MCP Servers at Scale
abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes how AI agents invoke external tools. MCP servers expose tools through a declared contract consisting of a name, description, and argument schema. In typical local deployments, client-side approval of a tool call grants the underlying server process broad host filesystem permissions rather than restricting it to the declared operation. We study the resulting vulnerability class, filesystem capability laundering, where attacker-steered arguments cause a tool to access sensitive host files outside its declared contract and deployment scope. We analyze this capability gap across three layers: server-category screening (L1), per-tool contract analysis (L2), and bypassable path-validation checks (L3). We design MCP-FSD to catalog MCP servers, infer least-privilege boundaries per tool, plant credential fixtures outside those boundaries, and evaluate exploitability and sandbox containment via paired dynamic execution. Across 21,097 MCP servers from nine registries, 787 of 4,806 triaged servers (16.4%) exhibit filesystem capabilities despite non-filesystem functional classifications. Dynamic three-case validation confirms 150 vulnerable instances under tested sandbox policies. Coordinated disclosure yielded 13 security advisories, including two CVEs in Anthropic's Git MCP Server.

title: Adding Temperature to the Adiabatic Connection: Hybrid Functionals for Static and Dynamic Correlation
abstract: Capturing static and dynamic electron correlation simultaneously at manageable computational cost remains a key challenge in electronic structure theory. Motivated by the recurring role of effective temperature in self-consistent field methods we extend the adiabatic connection mechanism from density functional theory to include a temperature dimension. This gives rise to thermally enhanced hybrid functionals, in which static correlation is captured via fractional occupations generated by an effective "correlation temperature" within thermal Hartree-Fock, while dynamic correlation is described by established density functional approximations. The framework formally unifies information-density matrix functional theory (i-DMFT) and thermally-assisted-occupation (TAO-)DFT as special cases, clarifying their theoretical basis and the respective prescriptions for the temperature parameter. We assess the performance of several thermally enhanced hybrids for different cases where i-DMFT was previously shown to fail. Furthermore, we discuss and test different schemes for determining the correlation temperature and investigate the accuracy of different such choices for a benchmark set derived from biphenyl. The results help to clarify the achievable balance of accuracy, generality, and efficiency, establishing thermally enhanced hybrids as a systematic route toward low-cost treatment of both correlation types.

title: International Multi-Centre Validation of Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Precise Discrimination between Normal and Abnormal Retinal Development
abstract: Arrested retinal development can cause childhood visual impairment, but grading optical coherence tomography scans is difficult to standardise across devices and centres. We developed and evaluated an unsupervised domain adaptation model to classify normal and abnormal retinal development across different OCT systems. This retrospective multicentre study used OCT scans from five centres in four countries and the UK Biobank. Data covered four OCT devices, including table mounted and handheld systems. A ResNet50 based Domain Adversarial Neural Network was trained using labelled images from a source device and unlabelled images from a target device. We evaluated six source to target pairings and compared model performance with seven clinician graders. A separate Heidelberg Spectralis dataset was reserved for external evaluation. Across validation sets, accuracy ranged from 87.75% to 96.06%, sensitivity from 88.68% to 98.38%, and specificity from 78.00% to 98.02%. The best performing model, adapted from TM OCT1 to HH OCT1, achieved 96.06% accuracy and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.994, with a 95% confidence interval from 0.981 to 0.999. Several models also maintained discrimination on the unseen Heidelberg device. Unsupervised domain adaptation enabled OCT classification across devices without labelled target device data. The approach may support more consistent assessment of retinal development and large scale analysis of existing imaging datasets.

title: RLDF: A Region-Level Deepfake Dataset and Benchmark for Partial-Face Manipulation Detection
abstract: Existing deepfake detection models are built upon manipu- lated images that are tampered with either exclusively fully swapped or fully synthesised faces, which leads us to an open question: Can off-the-shelf deepfake models detect manipulation effectively while tampering is confined to a local facial sub-region? To fill this gap, we introduce RLDF (Region-Level Deepfake), the first dataset for region-level deepfake evaluation. Employing the proposed region-aware partial swap synthesis model, we generate over 2M par- tial face-swap images by using eight face-swapping meth- ods. Altogether, we considered seven face regions, among which there are four discrete regions (eye, nose, mouth and eyebrow) and four composite facial regions (eye and nose; eye, nose and mouth; eye, nose, mouth and eye- brow; and full face). In addition, we define three evalu- ation protocols and benchmark 12 state-of-the-art detectors across the five popular standard cross-dataset evaluations, DF40, and the proposed RLDF, providing a comprehen- sive audit of where and why existing detectors underper- formed. Our evaluation reveals that existing detectors fail to generalize consistently across partial facial regions, re- sulting in an overall drop of 10.5% AUC and 10% accu- racy under region-level evaluation. Further, we propose a mask-guided cross-attention model as a baseline approach that can effectively detect region-level manipulation. The proposed dataset, code, and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/RLDF-Dataset/RLDF.
